definition_zh: 横幅；旗帜；标语
definition_en: a long strip of cloth with a message, or a flag
core_image: 体育馆外墙垂下一条红底白字的横幅
scene: 校门口挂起了新的标语。 A long banner hung across the street.
sceneCN: 这里 banner 是「横幅」（第 1 个义项：印有文字的长条布幅）；句意是一条长横幅横挂在街上。

derivatives.zh: banner 的复数形式，义为「横幅（复数）」

senses.title: A long strip with a message
senses.definition: a long piece of cloth or paper carrying a slogan or advertisement
senses.definitionCN: 印有标语或广告的长条布或纸
senses.example: A long banner hung across the street.
senses.exampleCN: 一条长横幅横挂在街上。
senses.why: Banner came from Old French baniere, a sign on cloth, so it began as something displayed to be read.

senses.title: A flag
senses.definition: a flag that represents a group or a cause
senses.definitionCN: 代表某个团体或事业的旗帜
senses.example: The team marched behind its banner.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍跟着自己的旗帜行进。
senses.why: A banner and a flag both mark who belongs together, so the words overlap for group signs.
senses.whyCN: 横幅与旗帜都标记「谁属于一起」，所以在表示团体标志时两词相通。

definition_zh: 最新的；最近的；最晚的；（the latest）最新消息
definition_en: the most recent or newest in a series, and as a noun the most recent news or information
core_image: 一叠报纸里最上面那张，油墨还没干
scene: 发布会开始前，编辑室里的人都在反复刷新页面。 She checked the latest report before the meeting began.
sceneCN: 这里 latest 指「最新的、最近的」（第 1 个义项）；句意为开会前她查看了最新的报告。图中可辨识物件：报纸、刷新中的屏幕、会议桌。

derivatives.zh: latest 的原级，意为「晚的；迟的」
由 late 加 -ness 构成，指迟到、偏晚的状态
late 的比较级，意为「后来；较晚地」

senses.title: The most recent in time
senses.definition: happening or produced most recently, so that nothing newer is available yet
senses.definitionCN: 最近发生或产生的，指目前还没有更新的同类事物
senses.example: She checked the latest report before the meeting began.
senses.exampleCN: 开会前她查看了最新的报告。
senses.why: The superlative ending marks the last point reached so far, so latest naturally becomes the most recent item in a series.
senses.whyCN: 最高级词尾标出到目前为止走到了最后一点，因此 latest 自然成为一系列中最新的那一项。

senses.title: The newest or most up-to-date
senses.definition: newest in design or style, as opposed to older versions of the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 在设计或款式上最新的，相对于同一事物的旧版本
senses.example: The shop window displayed the latest model of the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 橱窗里展示着这款手机的最新机型。
senses.why: When things are replaced by better versions, the newest one is also the one that came last, so the time sense doubles as a sense of style.
senses.whyCN: 当物品被更好的版本取代，最新的一款也正好是最后出现的那一款，于是时间义兼任「新式」义。

senses.title: The most recent news
senses.definition: the newest information or news about something, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 关于某事的最新信息或消息，作名词使用
senses.example: Have you heard the latest about the merger?
senses.exampleCN: 你听说合并的最新消息了吗？
senses.why: Newspapers turned the adjective into a noun: whatever is printed last is the latest that readers can get.
senses.whyCN: 报纸把这个形容词变成名词：最后印出来的那一条，就是读者能拿到的最新消息。

intro.en: Latest is the superlative of late, an Old English word for slow or tardy that later took on the sense of recent.
intro.cn: latest 是 late 的最高级；late 是古英语中表示迟缓的词，后来获得「最近」的意思。

items.en: Læt meant slow or sluggish, and it could describe a person who arrived after the expected time.
items.cn: læt 意为迟缓、懒散，也可形容超过预期时间才到的人。

items.en: The superlative ending -ost, later -est, produced the form latost, which became latest.
items.cn: 古英语最高级词尾 -ost（后为 -est）造出 latost，后来变成 latest。

items.en: Middle English used latest for the last in time as well as the most recent, and the two ideas still sit close together.
items.cn: 中古英语 latest 既指时间上最后的，也指最近的，这两种意思至今仍靠得很近。

items.en: Printing and newspapers gave the adjective a strong noun use, so the latest came to mean the newest news.
items.cn: 印刷与报纸让这个形容词有了稳固的名词用法，the latest 于是指最新消息。

items.en: Modern English keeps latest for the most recent item in a series, and at the latest for the final acceptable time.
items.cn: 现代英语用 latest 指一系列中最近的一项，at the latest 指最迟可接受的时间。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the late family and its comparative and superlative forms; the near-meaning group collects words for what is current or newest.
note.cn: 形近组收 late 一词族及其比较级、最高级形式；近义组收表示当前或最新事物的词。

entries.definition: After the expected time, the positive form behind latest.
entries.definitionCN: 晚于预期时间的，是 latest 的原级。

entries.definition: Showing the newest information or style.

normalIntro.en: The word is the superlative of an old adjective for slowness, and it now points at whatever came last and is therefore newest.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个古老「迟缓」形容词的最高级，如今指向最后出现、因而最新的事物。

normal.en: Late first meant slow, and only later did it mean after the expected time.
normal.cn: late 起初意为缓慢，后来才表示「晚于预期」。

normal.en: The ending -est builds the superlative, so latest is the most late, the last to arrive so far.
normal.cn: 词尾 -est 构成最高级，所以 latest 就是「最晚」，到目前为止最后到来的。

normal.en: The latest news is simply the last news printed, which is why an adjective became a noun.
normal.cn: the latest news 就是最后印出的消息，这就是形容词变名词的原因。

normal.en: At the latest sets a final deadline: no later than that moment.
normal.cn: at the latest 设定最后期限：不迟于那一刻。

normal.en: The latest model is newest because it arrived last in the line of versions.
normal.cn: the latest model 之所以最新，是因为它在一连串版本中最后出现。

abstract.en: Time and newness share one word because the newest thing is always the one that just arrived.
abstract.cn: 时间与新鲜共用一个词，因为最新的东西总是刚刚到来的那一个。

abstract.en: A superlative always draws a line around the present moment: after this, nothing newer is known.
abstract.cn: 最高级总在此刻画一条线：在此之后，还不知道有更新的东西。

abstract.en: A newspaper prints last and still calls itself the latest, because freshness is a race, not a fact.
abstract.cn: 报纸最后付印，却仍称自己最新，因为新鲜是一场赛跑，而不是一个事实。

examples.cn: 开会前她查看了最新的报告。

examples.en: Please arrive by nine at the latest.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累停」——最新消息太多，人累得停下来；谐音记住 latest 是最新的。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是到目前为止抵达的最后一点；由此分出「最近的」「最新款」与「最新消息」。

definition_zh: 心爱的；深受爱戴的
definition_en: much loved by someone

scene: 老人把那张旧照片放在枕边。 She kept a photo of her beloved husband.

definition_zh: 唤醒；激起；使振奋；鼓动
definition_en: to wake someone, to stir a feeling, or to urge someone into action
core_image: 清晨吹响的号角
scene: 号角声唤醒了沉睡的营地。 The bugle roused the sleeping camp.
sceneCN: 这里 rouse 是「唤醒」（第 1 个义项）；句意：号角声唤醒了沉睡的营地。

senses.title: Wake up
senses.definition: to wake someone from sleep
senses.definitionCN: 把某人从睡梦中叫醒
senses.example: The noise roused him from a deep sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 噪声把他从沉睡中唤醒。
senses.why: The sleeper is shaken out of rest.
senses.whyCN: 沉睡者被从休息中摇醒。

senses.title: Stir feeling
senses.definition: to cause a strong feeling or interest
senses.definitionCN: 引发强烈的情感或兴趣
senses.example: The speech roused anger in the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲激起了人群的愤怒。
senses.why: A feeling is woken up like a sleeper.
senses.whyCN: 情感像沉睡者一样被唤醒。

senses.title: Urge to act
senses.definition: to make someone ready to do something
senses.definitionCN: 使某人准备好采取行动
senses.example: The news roused the town to action.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息鼓动全镇行动起来。
senses.why: People are moved from rest into motion.
senses.whyCN: 人们被从静止推向行动。

items.en: Ruser means to drive back or startle.
items.cn: ruser 意为赶回或使惊起。

normal.en: The coach roused the team before the match.

branches.cn: 情感也能被唤醒。

branches.en: People are roused into action.
branches.cn: 人们被鼓动起来行动。

branches.en: Both move something from rest to response.
branches.cn: 两者都把某物从静止推向反应。

branches.en: Stirred feeling leads to action.
branches.cn: 被激起的情感导向行动。

intro.en: Rouse comes from Old French ruser and builds English forms.
intro.cn: rouse 来自古法语 ruser，并在英语中派生新词。

latinIntro.en: Rouse has no Latin root; the path runs through French.
latinIntro.cn: rouse 没有拉丁词根，其路径经过法语。

items.exampleCN: rousing 形容振奋人心的演讲。

definition_zh: 穿透；渗入；洞察；打入（市场）
definition_en: to pass into or through something solid, to spread through a material, to see into something hidden, or to enter a market or group that is hard to reach
core_image: 一根细针顶住表面，慢慢从另一侧露出来
scene: 手术台的灯下，医生把细长的针尖抵住皮肤，缓缓向下推进。 The needle penetrated the skin without waking the patient.
sceneCN: 这里是「穿透、刺入」（第 1 个义项：穿过实体屏障）；句意为针头穿过皮肤，病人没有被惊醒。

derivatives.zh: 由动词 penetrate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「穿透；渗透；洞察力」
由现在分词转化而来，义为「有穿透力的；尖锐的」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可被穿透的」
加后缀 -ive 构成，义为「有渗透力的」

senses.title: To pass into or through something solid
senses.definition: to make a way into or through a solid object, often by force or with a sharp point
senses.definitionCN: 进入或穿过坚固物体，常靠外力或尖锐的端点
senses.example: The drill penetrated the concrete wall in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 钻头几秒钟就穿透了混凝土墙。
senses.why: The Latin verb penetrare described going into a body that resists, so the earliest sense is a pointed or forceful entry through a barrier.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 penetrare 描述的是进入一个有阻力的物体内部，所以最早的意思是带尖端或靠力量的进入，穿过一道屏障。

senses.title: To spread through a material
senses.definition: to spread through the small spaces of a material, as a liquid, gas or smell does
senses.definitionCN: 像液体、气体或气味那样，通过材料内部的细小空隙扩散开来
senses.example: Smoke had penetrated every room of the building.
senses.exampleCN: 烟已经渗进大楼的每个房间。
senses.why: A liquid or smell does not need one clean hole; it works through tiny gaps, and that slow spreading is the second face of the same entering action.
senses.whyCN: 液体或气味不需要一个整齐的洞，而是从细微的缝隙里钻过去；这种缓慢的扩散，就是「进入」这个动作的第二张面孔。

senses.title: To see into something hidden
senses.definition: to see through a disguise, a plan or a mystery and understand what is really there
senses.definitionCN: 看穿伪装、计划或谜团，理解其中真正的东西
senses.example: Her calm questions penetrated his carefully built excuse.
senses.exampleCN: 她平静的追问看穿了他精心编造的借口。
senses.why: English treats sight as something that reaches inside a thing, so the verb of going through a wall becomes the verb of going through a lie.
senses.whyCN: 英语把目光看成能伸进事物内部的东西，于是「穿墙」的动词也成了「看穿谎言」的动词。

senses.title: To enter a market or a closed group
senses.definition: to get into a market, an organization or a group that outsiders find hard to reach
senses.definitionCN: 进入外人难以触及的市场、机构或群体
senses.example: The brand took ten years to penetrate the local market.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌花了十年才打入当地市场。
senses.why: A market or a club is imagined as a closed body with a wall around it, so getting inside is pictured as the same act of pushing through.
senses.whyCN: 市场和圈子被想象成有围墙的封闭身体，于是「进去」就被画成同一个往里挤的动作。

intro.en: Penetrate comes straight from Latin, where a word for the inner part of a house grew into a verb for going inside anything.
intro.cn: penetrate 直接来自拉丁语：一个表示房屋最里侧的词，长成了表示「进入任何东西内部」的动词。

items.en: Penus named the inner store of a house, the part where food and valuables were kept; the link to the verb is generally accepted but not certain.
items.cn: penus 指房屋最里侧的储藏处，存放食物和贵重物品的地方；它与动词的联系一般认为成立，但并非定论。

items.en: The adverb penitus meant inward, deep inside, and it supplied the picture of a point moving toward the middle.
items.cn: 副词 penitus 意为向内、在深处，提供了「一个点朝中心移动」的画面。

items.en: Penetrare meant to enter, pierce or pass through, and Roman writers used it for armies, weapons and even arguments.
items.cn: penetrare 意为进入、刺穿、穿过，罗马作家用它写军队、武器，甚至写论证。

items.en: English borrowed the verb directly from Latin in the sixteenth century, first for physical piercing and soon for understanding.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪直接从拉丁语借入这个动词，先指身体上的刺穿，很快又用于理解。

items.en: Modern English uses it for liquids in walls, ideas in minds and products in markets, all as versions of one act.
items.cn: 现代英语用它说墙里的液体、脑子里的观念、市场上的产品，全都是同一个动作的不同版本。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group collects verbs of piercing, seeping and getting inside.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示刺入、渗出与进入内部的动词。

entries.definition: The act of passing into or through something, or the ability to see deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 穿入或穿过的动作，也指看得很深的能力。

entries.definition: Able to pass through, or sharp and full of insight.
entries.definitionCN: 能穿过的；尖锐而有洞察力的。

entries.definition: Possible to pass through or get into.
Having the power to pass into something deeply.
To make a hole in something with a sharp point.
entries.definitionCN: 用尖物在某物上扎出孔。

entries.definition: To flow slowly through small openings.
entries.definitionCN: 从细小开口缓慢流出或渗入。

entries.definition: To spread through every part of something.
entries.definitionCN: 扩散到某物的每个部分。

entries.definition: To enter an organization or place secretly.
entries.definitionCN: 秘密进入某个组织或地方。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin stem for the inner part, and its family keeps returning to the act of getting inside something.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「最里侧」的拉丁词干上，同族词反复回到「进入内部」这个动作。

normal.en: Penitus in Latin means deep inside, and penetrate still carries that inward direction.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 penitus 意为「在深处」，penetrate 至今保留着这个向内的方向。

normal.en: The ending -ate marks a Latin verb, so penetrate behaves like a doing word, not a naming word.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 是拉丁动词的标志，所以 penetrate 是「做」的词，不是「命名」的词。

normal.en: Add -ion and you get penetration, the act itself; add -ing and you get the quality of getting through.
normal.cn: 加 -ion 得到 penetration，指动作本身；加 -ing 得到「能穿过去」的性质。

normal.en: Pierce is a single sharp hole, while penetrate can also mean spreading through a whole material.
normal.cn: pierce 是一个尖锐的孔，penetrate 还能表示浸透整块材料。

normal.en: A company that penetrates a market is doing to the market what a needle does to cloth.
normal.cn: 企业「打入市场」，对市场做的正是针对于布做的事。

abstract.en: To penetrate is to refuse to stop at the surface, whether the surface is a wall, a rumour or a face.
abstract.cn: 穿透就是不肯停在表面，不管表面是墙、是传言，还是一张脸。

abstract.en: The same word covers a needle, a smell and an argument because all three leave the outside and reach the inside.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能覆盖针、气味和论证，因为这三者都离开外部、抵达内部。

abstract.en: A market is treated as a body with skin, which is why selling is described with the language of surgery.
abstract.cn: 市场被当成有皮肤的身体，所以销售也用外科手术的语言来描述。

examples.en: The arrow penetrated the wooden shield and stuck fast.
examples.cn: 箭穿透木盾，牢牢钉住。

examples.en: Cold air penetrated the thin walls of the hut.
examples.cn: 冷空气渗进小屋薄薄的墙。

examples.en: Few reporters have penetrated the secretive world of the firm.
examples.cn: 很少有记者能进入这家公司隐秘的世界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮内戳的」——针尖戳进皮肉里面，就是穿透；记住 penetrate。

root: 拉丁语 penus（房屋最里侧的储藏处）经副词 penitus（向内、在深处）发展出动词 penetrare（进入、穿透）；英语十六世纪直接借入，同族词多与「进入内部」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core act is getting inside; the senses differ only in what is being entered, a solid object, a material, a hidden truth or a market.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心动作是「进入内部」；各义项的差别只在进入的是什么——固体、材料、隐情，还是市场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine needle pressing on a surface and showing up on the other side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细针压住表面，从另一侧露出来。

branches.en: a needle sliding through leather
branches.cn: 针穿过皮革

branches.en: rain working its way through roof tiles
branches.cn: 雨水从瓦片间渗下去

branches.en: a stare that strips away an excuse
branches.cn: 一眼看掉借口

branches.en: a brand pushing into a guarded market
branches.cn: 品牌挤进被守住的市场

branches.en: from breaking a surface to breaking a lie
branches.cn: 从破开表面到破开谎言

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin adverb for the inner part, its verb of entering, and a set of Latin and English endings that turn it into a noun and qualities.
intro.cn: 这个词依托拉丁语中表示「里侧」的副词、表示「进入」的动词，以及一组把它变成名词和性质词的拉丁、英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on penitus, inward, and the verb penetrare, to enter; the noun penetratio names the act.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 penitus（向内）与动词 penetrare（进入）之上；名词 penetratio 表示进入这一动作。

items.meaning: act or result of an action

items.meaningCN: 形容词后缀：具有做……的性质

definition_zh: 不久；很快；目前；现在
definition_en: after a short time; also at the present time or moment
core_image: 一个人站在站台边看表，说再等一会儿就出发，而此刻他还站在原地
scene: 火车站的广播刚响过，朋友还没到，他看了看表，对电话那头说再等一会儿就好。 The train will leave presently, so stay near the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 presently 指「不久、很快」（第 1 个义项：在很短时间之后）；句意为列车很快就要开了，所以别走远。图中可辨识物件：站台、时钟、行李箱。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 praesens 进入英语的形容词，义为「现在的；出席的」，是 presently 的词干
由拉丁 praesentia 进入英语，义为「在场；出席」，与 presently 同源
由 present 与 day 复合而成，义为「当今的；当前的」

senses.title: After a short time
senses.definition: at a time not long from now, or soon after a point in the past
senses.definitionCN: 在离现在不远的将来，或在过去某一时点之后不久
senses.example: The doctor will see you presently.
senses.exampleCN: 医生很快就会给你看诊。
senses.why: The base word describes what is here and now, and the -ly ending turns that nearness into a point just ahead of now, so the word points to a moment slightly in front of the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 词干描述「就在眼前、就在此刻」，-ly 把这种贴近感变成一个时间点：事情已经贴近眼前，发生的时刻就在稍前一点，于是产生「不久、很快」的用法，重心落在说话之后的短时间里。

senses.title: At the present time
senses.definition: at this moment or during the current period
senses.definitionCN: 在此刻或当前这段时期
senses.example: The office is presently closed for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室目前因维修关闭。
senses.why: Because present already means what exists now, the adverb can simply stand for at this time, and this reading has become the dominant one in modern American usage.
senses.whyCN: present 本身就指「此刻存在的」，副词直接取其「现在」一义即可；现代美式英语里这个读法已经压过「不久」，成为最常用的理解，所以同一拼写要按上下文分辨。

intro.en: Presently is present plus the adverb ending -ly; the base goes back to a Latin adjective for what is in front of someone, and the adverb splits between soon and now.
intro.cn: presently 是 present 加副词后缀 -ly；词干可追到表示「在某人面前」的拉丁形容词，副词义则在「不久」与「现在」之间分叉。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, and it placed the word at the near edge of a scene.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，把词义放在场景的近处边缘。

items.en: The verb esse meant to be or to exist, and its participle supplied the idea of something actually being there.
items.cn: 动词 esse 意为「存在、是」，其分词提供了「确实在那里」这一层意思。

items.en: Praesens described a person or thing that is here in front of the eyes, and it became the English adjective present.
items.cn: praesens 描述就在眼前的人或物，后来成为英语形容词 present。

items.en: Middle English joined present with the native adverb ending -ly, and the new word could already mean both at this time and after a little while.
items.cn: 中古英语把 present 与本地副词后缀 -ly 结合，新词当时已兼指「此时」与「过一会儿」。

items.en: British usage long favoured the sense soon, while American usage settled on at the present time, so the adverb now needs context to be read correctly.
items.cn: 英式用法长期偏向「不久」，美式用法则固定在「目前」，所以今天读到这个词要依靠上下文判断。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the present family built on Latin praesens; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of time close to now.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语 praesens 衍生出的 present 词族展开；近义组收表示「靠近此刻」的时间副词。

entries.definition: Being here now, or the current period.
entries.definitionCN: 现在的；在场的；当前时期。

entries.definition: The state of being in a place.
A talk that shows and explains something.
entries.definitionCN: 展示并讲解某事的报告。

entries.definition: After a short time from now.
entries.definitionCN: 从现在起很短时间之后；不久。

entries.definition: In a little while, or briefly.

normalIntro.en: The word is the adjective present bent into an adverb; its family keeps circling the idea of being here, at this point in time.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由形容词 present 折成副词；同族词始终围绕「就在这里、就在此刻」展开。

normal.en: Presently is present plus -ly, so the adverb keeps the idea of what is here at this moment.
normal.cn: presently 是 present 加 -ly，所以副词保留了「此刻就在这里」的意思。

normal.en: The same ending -ly appears in quickly and slowly, turning an adjective into a word about time or manner.
normal.cn: 同样的 -ly 也出现在 quickly 与 slowly 里，把形容词变成表示时间或方式的词。

normal.en: Presence and presently share praesens: one names being here, the other names the time around here.
normal.cn: presence 与 presently 共用 praesens：一个指「在这里」，另一个指「这附近的时间」。

normal.en: In British writing presently often means soon, while in American writing it usually means now, so the sentence, not the spelling, decides.
normal.cn: 英式写作里 presently 常指「不久」，美式写作里多指「现在」，所以决定词义的是句子而不是拼写。

normal.en: The phrase presently available is a safe test: it almost always means available now, not available soon.
normal.cn: presently available 是个稳妥的检验：它几乎总指「现在就可用的」，而不是「很快可用」。

abstract.en: A word that means both soon and now shows how thin the line is between the moment just ahead and the moment we already stand in.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时表示「不久」和「现在」，说明「即将到来」与「已经身处其中」之间只隔一条很细的线。

abstract.en: Presently is what happens when a word for being here is bent into a word for time.
abstract.cn: presently 就是一个表示「在这里」的词被折成表示时间的词之后的样子。

abstract.en: Reading presently correctly means asking where the speaker is standing: before the event, or inside it.
abstract.cn: 要读对 presently，就得问说话人站在哪里：事件之前，还是事件之中。

examples.en: The doctor will see you presently.
examples.cn: 医生很快就会给你看诊。

examples.en: The office is presently closed for repairs.
examples.cn: 办公室目前因维修关闭。

examples.en: All presently available seats are listed on the board.
examples.cn: 目前可用的座位都列在牌子上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞怎特利」——先「在眼前」，再「马上来」；谐音只助记，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ esse（存在）→ praesens（在场的）→ 英语 present + 副词后缀 -ly → presently；词干义为「此刻在眼前」，副词由此兼指「现在」与「不久」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is nearness in time; one branch leans forward to a moment shortly after now, the other stays on the current moment.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是时间上的「贴近」；一条分支向前指说话之后不久的时点，另一条停在当前这一刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a station looking at a watch, saying the train comes in a moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：站台上的人看着表，说列车一会儿就到。

branches.en: a sign reading closed for repairs
branches.cn: 写着维修期间暂停开放的告示

branches.en: a train announced a few minutes away
branches.cn: 广播说还有几分钟到站的列车

branches.en: a desk still holding today's papers
branches.cn: 桌上还摊着今天的文件

branches.en: a kettle just starting to whistle
branches.cn: 刚开始鸣叫的水壶

branches.en: a question left unanswered for now
branches.cn: 暂时没有答案的问题

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of presence plus an English adverb ending, and the family keeps the same two pieces.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示「在场」的拉丁形容词加英语副词后缀，整个词族都保留这两块构件。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: in the manner of, at the time of

definition_zh: 和谐；协调；和睦
definition_en: a pleasing combination of sounds, or a peaceful and balanced relationship
core_image: 几把不同的乐器同时奏出同一个和弦
scene: 几个声部合在一起很和谐。 The voices blended in harmony.
sceneCN: 这里 harmony 是「和谐」（第 1 个义项）；句意：几个声部合在一起很和谐。

senses.title: Pleasing sound
senses.definition: a combination of musical notes that sounds pleasant together
senses.definitionCN: 同时发声而听起来悦耳的音符组合
senses.example: The voices blended in harmony.
senses.exampleCN: 几个声部合在一起很和谐。
senses.why: This is the musical origin sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是源自音乐的义项。

senses.title: Things fitting together
senses.definition: a state in which different parts fit well together
senses.definitionCN: 不同部分彼此契合的状态
senses.example: The colours are in harmony.
senses.exampleCN: 这些颜色很协调。
senses.why: Pleasing notes became pleasing parts.
senses.whyCN: 悦耳的音，变成了悦目的搭配。

senses.title: Peace between people
senses.definition: a peaceful relationship without fighting
senses.definitionCN: 没有争斗的和平关系
senses.example: The two families live in harmony.
senses.exampleCN: 两家人和睦相处。
senses.why: Parts that fit in sound also fit in society.
senses.whyCN: 声音里契合的部分，也能在社会里契合。

intro.en: Harmony comes from Greek harmonia, a joining together.
intro.cn: harmony 来自希腊语 harmonia，意为连接、结合。

items.en: Harmonia meant a fitting together.
items.cn: harmonia 意为契合连接。

items.en: Harmonia entered Latin as harmony of sound.
items.cn: harmonia 在拉丁语中指声音的和谐。

items.en: The word reached English through French.
items.cn: 这个词经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Harmony named music and then agreement.
items.cn: harmony 先指音乐，后指一致。

items.en: It came to mean peace among people.
items.cn: 它进而指人与人之间的和睦。

note.en: Harmony is compared with look-alike words and with words for agreement and peace.
note.cn: 把 harmony 与形近词以及表示一致和和平的词作比较。

entries.definition: the state of having the same view

normalIntro.en: Harmony began as notes that fit and became people who fit.
normalIntro.cn: harmony 起初是彼此相合的音，后来成了彼此相合的人。

normal.en: The choir sang in harmony.
normal.cn: 合唱团和谐地演唱。

normal.en: The garden is in harmony with the house.
normal.cn: 花园与房子很协调。

normal.en: They lived in harmony for years.
normal.cn: 他们多年和睦相处。

normal.en: We must work in harmony.
normal.cn: 我们必须协调一致地工作。

normal.en: Peace and harmony returned to the town.
normal.cn: 和平与和睦回到了小镇。

abstract.en: Harmony is difference that has agreed to cooperate.
abstract.cn: 和谐，是差异同意合作。

abstract.en: One voice alone has no harmony to offer.
abstract.cn: 单独一个声音，给不出和声。

abstract.en: The sweetest sound is many sounds that do not fight.
abstract.cn: 最甜的声音，是许多不打架的声音。

examples.en: The voices blended in harmony.
examples.cn: 几个声部合在一起很和谐。

examples.en: The colours are in harmony.
examples.cn: 这些颜色很协调。

examples.en: The two families live in harmony.
examples.cn: 两家人和睦相处。

dict_mnemonic.text: harmony 来自希腊语「连接」，先指声音的「和声、和谐」，再指颜色的「协调」与人际的「和睦」；in harmony with 是与……和谐一致。

root: 希腊语 harmonia（契合、连接）经拉丁语与法语进入英语；由和声的悦耳，引申为部分之间的协调与人际的和睦。

sensesIntro.en: Harmony is notes that sound well, parts that fit well, or people who live well together.
sensesIntro.cn: harmony 是悦耳的音、契合的部分，或和睦相处的人。

core.en: Two notes that meet and do not clash.
core.cn: 两个相遇而不冲突的音。

branches.en: A choir holds one long chord.
branches.cn: 合唱团保持一个长和弦。

branches.en: Curtains and walls share one colour.
branches.cn: 窗帘与墙共享一种颜色。

branches.en: Two neighbours share a fence and a meal.
branches.cn: 两家邻居共用一道篱笆和一餐饭。

branches.en: Sound and sight can both be tuned.
branches.cn: 声音与视觉，都能被调准。

branches.en: Things that fit make people who fit.
branches.cn: 彼此契合的东西，造就彼此契合的人。

intro.en: Harmony builds adjectives with -ious and a verb with -ize.
intro.cn: harmony 加 -ious 构成形容词，加 -ize 构成动词。

latinIntro.en: The Greek base harmonia means a joining.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词基 harmonia 意为连接。

items.example: The room is full of harmony.

items.exampleCN: 他们把两个方案协调起来。

definition_zh: 简化；使简易
definition_en: to make something easier to understand or do
core_image: 一团缠结的线被慢慢理成一条直线
scene: 老师把复杂的规则简化成三条。 The teacher simplified the complex rules into three points.
sceneCN: 这里 simplify 是「简化」（第 1 个义项）；句意：老师把复杂的规则简化成三条。

senses.title: To make easier to understand
senses.definition: to make something less difficult to understand
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物不那么难懂
senses.example: The teacher simplified the complex rules into three points.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把复杂的规则简化成三条。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of making ideas easier.
senses.whyCN: 这是把想法变容易的日常义项。

senses.title: To make less complex
senses.definition: to remove parts so that a thing works more simply
senses.definitionCN: 去掉部分零件，使事物运作更简单
senses.example: The new app simplifies the booking process.
senses.exampleCN: 新应用简化了预订流程。
senses.why: The same action applies to objects and systems.
senses.whyCN: 同样的动作也适用于物品和系统。

intro.en: Simplify joins the Latin words for simple and to make.
intro.cn: simplify 由拉丁语中表示「简单」和「做」的词组合而成。

items.en: Simplus meant simple or single.
items.cn: simplus 意为简单的或单一的。

items.en: Facere meant to make or do.
items.cn: facere 意为制作或做。

items.en: Simplifier meant to make simple.
items.cn: simplifier 意为使简单。

items.en: English borrowed it as simplifien.
items.cn: 英语借入时写作 simplifien。

items.en: The spelling became simplify.
items.cn: 拼写最终变为 simplify。

note.en: Simplify is compared with similar-looking verbs and with verbs for making clear.
note.cn: 把 simplify 与形近动词以及表示澄清的动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: To simplify is to give less, but let more be understood.
normalIntro.cn: simplify 就是减少内容，却让人听懂更多。

normal.en: The teacher simplified the complex rules into three points.
normal.cn: 老师把复杂的规则简化成三条。

normal.en: The new app simplifies the booking process.
normal.cn: 新应用简化了预订流程。

normal.en: We need to simplify the form before printing it.
normal.cn: 打印之前我们需要简化这张表格。

normal.en: He simplified his speech for younger listeners.
normal.cn: 他为了让年轻听众听懂而简化了讲稿。

normal.en: Good design simplifies daily life.
normal.cn: 好的设计能简化日常生活。

abstract.en: Simplification is the art of keeping what matters.
abstract.cn: 简化是保留真正重要之物的艺术。

abstract.en: A simple line can hold a whole story.
abstract.cn: 一条简单的线也能承载整个故事。

abstract.en: Taking away can be a form of giving.
abstract.cn: 拿走一些东西，也可以是一种给予。

examples.en: The teacher simplified the complex rules into three points.
examples.cn: 老师把复杂的规则简化成三条。

examples.en: The new app simplifies the booking process.
examples.cn: 新应用简化了预订流程。

examples.en: He simplified his speech for younger listeners.
examples.cn: 他为了让年轻听众听懂而简化了讲稿。

dict_mnemonic.text: simple（简单的）+ -ify（使……）= simplify，字面就是「使简单」；同类动词还有 clarify（使清楚）、beautify（美化）。

root: 源自拉丁语 simplus（简单的）加 facere（做），经古法语 simplifier 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Simplify means to make something easier to understand or less complex.
sensesIntro.cn: simplify 意为使某事物更容易理解或更不复杂。

core.en: Reduce complication so that the point shows.
core.cn: 减少复杂之处，让要点显露。

branches.en: A complicated rule becomes three clear points.
branches.cn: 复杂规则变成三条清晰的要点。

branches.en: An app cuts steps from a booking flow.
branches.cn: 应用减少了预订流程的步骤。

branches.en: Ideas and systems can both be made simple.
branches.cn: 想法和系统都能被简化。

branches.en: A teacher speaks so that beginners follow.
branches.cn: 老师讲解得让初学者也能跟上。

branches.en: A design gives only what the user needs.
branches.cn: 设计只保留用户真正需要的部分。

intro.en: Simplify shows -ify turning an adjective into a verb.
intro.cn: simplify 展示了 -ify 如何把形容词变成动词。

latinIntro.en: Simplify comes from Latin simplus and facere.
latinIntro.cn: simplify 来自拉丁语 simplus 和 facere。

items.exampleCN: 这个设计真正做到了简洁。

definition_zh: 丝带；带状物；奖带
definition_en: a long narrow piece of cloth used for tying or decorating
core_image: 礼物盒上打成蝴蝶结的红色丝带
scene: 她把红色丝带系在礼物盒上，打了一个整齐的结。 She tied a red ribbon around the gift box and made a neat bow.
sceneCN: 这里 ribbon 是「丝带」（第 1 个义项：用于系扎或装饰的窄布条）；句意：她把红色丝带系在礼物盒上，打了一个整齐的结。

senses.title: Decorative band
senses.definition: a narrow band of cloth used to tie or decorate
senses.definitionCN: 用于系扎或装饰的窄布条
senses.example: The ribbon matched the color of the box.
senses.exampleCN: 丝带和盒子的颜色很相配。
senses.why: The word comes from French ruban, a silk band.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自法语 ruban（丝带）。

senses.title: Strip of material
senses.definition: a long narrow strip of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物的长窄条
senses.example: A ribbon of road followed the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一条带状公路沿着河延伸。
senses.why: Any long narrow strip can share the ribbon shape.
senses.whyCN: 任何细长条都能借用丝带的形状。

senses.title: Award band
senses.definition: a band given as a prize or mark of honor
senses.definitionCN: 作为奖品或荣誉标志的带子
senses.example: Her essay won a blue ribbon.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文章赢得了蓝带奖。
senses.why: Prize ribbons borrow the look of a tied band.
senses.whyCN: 奖带借用了系带的样式。

intro.en: Ribbon comes from Old French ruban, a silk band.
intro.cn: ribbon 源自法语 ruban（丝带）。

items.en: Ruban means a silk band.
items.cn: ruban 意为丝带。

items.en: The word names a fine narrow cloth.
items.cn: 这个词指精细的窄布。

items.en: Ribbon keeps the decorative sense.
items.cn: ribbon 保留了装饰性的含义。

items.en: It also names any narrow strip.
items.cn: 它也指任何窄条。

items.en: Prize ribbons are common at fairs.
items.cn: 集市上常见奖带。

note.en: Ribbon is a narrow cloth band; a strip can be any material.
note.cn: ribbon 是窄布带；strip 可以是任何材料。

entries.definition: a thin strip used to tie things
a long thin material used for fastening
a wide cloth band worn around the waist

normalIntro.en: Ribbon is a thin river of cloth tied into a bow.
normalIntro.cn: ribbon 是一条被打成蝴蝶结的细布河。

normal.en: Tie a ribbon around the box.
normal.cn: 在盒子上系一条丝带。

normal.en: Ribbon cutting marks a new opening.
normal.cn: 剪彩标志着新的开端。

normal.en: A blue ribbon is a prize at a fair.
normal.cn: 蓝带是集市上的奖品。

normal.en: A ribbon of road follows the valley.
normal.cn: 一条带状公路沿着山谷延伸。

normal.en: Compare band: a band may tie hair, a ribbon decorates.
normal.cn: 对比 band：band 可扎头发，ribbon 用于装饰。

abstract.en: Picture a red line tying two worlds together.
abstract.cn: 想象一条红线把两个世界系在一起。

abstract.en: Imagine a river seen from above as a silk thread.
abstract.cn: 想象从高处看，河流像一根丝线。

abstract.en: Think of a gift that becomes more precious with a bow.
abstract.cn: 想象一份因蝴蝶结而更显珍贵的礼物。

examples.en: She wore a yellow ribbon in her hair.
examples.cn: 她头发上系着一条黄丝带。

examples.en: The mayor cut the ribbon at the new library.
examples.cn: 市长在新图书馆剪彩。

examples.en: A ribbon of smoke rose from the chimney.
examples.cn: 一缕烟从烟囱里袅袅升起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ribbon」两段 b 相连——像一条被反复折叠、打成蝴蝶结的丝带。

root: 古法语 ruban（丝带）→ 中古英语 riban → ribbon，核心义「细长的布带及其相似物」。

sensesIntro.en: Ribbon begins as a decorative cloth band, extends to any narrow strip, and also names a prize band.
sensesIntro.cn: ribbon 先是装饰性的布带，再指任何窄条，也指奖品带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red ribbon tied into a bow on a gift box.
core.cn: 核心意象：礼物盒上打成蝴蝶结的红丝带。

branches.en: The decorative band is the core.
branches.cn: 装饰布带是核心含义。

branches.en: The narrow shape extends to other strips.
branches.cn: 窄长形状延伸到其他条状物。

branches.en: A prize band borrows the same form.
branches.cn: 奖带借用了同样的形态。

branches.en: Decorating and honoring both use a band.
branches.cn: 装饰与表彰都使用带子。

branches.en: A prize band and a strip share the narrow shape.
branches.cn: 奖带与条带共享窄长的形状。

intro.en: Ribbon comes from French and takes little English affixing.
intro.cn: ribbon 来自法语，英语中很少再加词缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is French in origin rather than Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自法语，而非拉丁语。

items.example: Riban is the older English spelling.
items.exampleCN: riban 是较早的英语拼写。
ribboned 描述装饰过的物品。

items.example: Ribbonlike describes a long narrow shape.

definition_zh: 熔炉；暖气炉；极热的地方
definition_en: a closed container or building in which great heat is produced, or a heating system for a building
core_image: 铁水在炽热的熔炉里翻滚发红
scene: 铁在炽热的熔炉里熔化。 Iron is melted in a hot furnace.
sceneCN: 这里 furnace 是「熔炉」（第 1 个义项）；句意：铁在炽热的熔炉里熔化。

senses.title: Chamber of great heat
senses.definition: a very hot enclosed space in which metal or glass is melted
senses.definitionCN: 用来熔化金属或玻璃的极热封闭空间
senses.example: Iron is melted in a hot furnace.
senses.exampleCN: 铁在炽热的熔炉里熔化。
senses.why: This is the industrial sense of intense heat.
senses.whyCN: 这是工业中表示高温设备的义项。

senses.title: Home heating system
senses.definition: a machine that heats a building by warming air or water
senses.definitionCN: 通过加热空气或水来给建筑物供暖的机器
senses.example: The furnace keeps the house warm in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 暖气炉让房子在冬天保持温暖。
senses.why: The same chamber idea moved into the home.
senses.whyCN: 同样的炉室概念进入了家庭。

senses.title: Very hot place
senses.definition: a place or situation that feels extremely hot
senses.definitionCN: 让人感到极其炎热的地方或处境
senses.example: The desert at noon was a furnace.
senses.exampleCN: 正午的沙漠就像一个熔炉。
senses.why: The word is used figuratively for heat.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被比喻性地用来形容酷热。

intro.en: Furnace goes back through Old French to a Latin word for an oven.
intro.cn: furnace 经古法语可追溯到拉丁语中表示炉子的词。

items.en: Fornax meant an oven or furnace.
items.cn: fornax 意为炉子或熔炉。

items.en: Fornase named a large oven.
items.cn: fornase 指大型炉子。

items.en: The word entered English as furnace.
items.cn: 这个词以 furnace 进入英语。

items.en: It named chambers for melting metal.
items.cn: 它指熔化金属的炉室。

items.en: It also named home heating systems.
items.cn: 它也指家庭供暖设备。

note.en: Furnace is compared with look-alike words and words for heating devices.
note.cn: 把 furnace 与形近词以及表示加热设备的词作比较。

entries.definition: a closed box for baking food

normalIntro.en: A furnace is a box or room built to hold great heat.
normalIntro.cn: furnace 是用来盛住高温的炉室。

normal.en: Iron is melted in a hot furnace.
normal.cn: 铁在炽热的熔炉里熔化。

normal.en: The furnace keeps the house warm in winter.
normal.cn: 暖气炉让房子在冬天保持温暖。

normal.en: The desert at noon was a furnace.
normal.cn: 正午的沙漠就像一个熔炉。

normal.en: Workers checked the furnace every hour.
normal.cn: 工人们每小时检查一次熔炉。

normal.en: A blast furnace turns ore into liquid metal.
normal.cn: 高炉把矿石变成铁水。

abstract.en: A furnace teaches that useful change needs heat.
abstract.cn: 熔炉说明有用的改变需要热量。

abstract.en: Some anger is a furnace with no door.
abstract.cn: 有些愤怒是一座没有门的熔炉。

abstract.en: The strongest metal remembers the hottest fire.
abstract.cn: 最坚固的金属记得最炽热的火。

examples.en: Iron is melted in a hot furnace.
examples.cn: 铁在炽热的熔炉里熔化。

examples.en: The furnace keeps the house warm in winter.
examples.cn: 暖气炉让房子在冬天保持温暖。

examples.en: The desert at noon was a furnace.
examples.cn: 正午的沙漠就像一个熔炉。

dict_mnemonic.text: furnace 与 furnish、furniture 同以 furn 开头；blast furnace 是「高炉」，furnace room 是「锅炉房」。

root: 经古法语 fornaise 来自拉丁语 fornax（炉子），核心义「容纳高温的炉室」。

sensesIntro.en: Furnace is an industrial melting chamber, a home heating unit, or any place of extreme heat.
sensesIntro.cn: furnace 指工业熔炉、家用暖气炉，或任何极热之处。

core.en: An enclosed space that holds intense heat.
core.cn: 容纳强烈高温的封闭空间。

branches.en: Ore becomes liquid inside the chamber.
branches.cn: 矿石在炉室里变成液体。

branches.en: Warm air rises through the house.
branches.cn: 暖空气在屋子里升起。

branches.en: Noon turns the desert into an oven.
branches.cn: 正午把沙漠变成烤箱。

branches.en: Industry and home share the heating box.
branches.cn: 工业与家庭共享这个加热的箱体。

branches.en: Real and imagined heat meet in one word.
branches.cn: 真实与想象中的高温在这个词里相遇。

intro.en: Furnace forms compounds for rooms, parts, and workers.
intro.cn: furnace 构成表示炉室、部件和工人的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root fornax also gave words for ovens.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 fornax 也衍生出表示炉子的词。

items.example: The furnace glowed red all night.

items.exampleCN: 这家工厂开动三座熔炉。

items.meaning: a worker who tends a furnace

items.example: The attic felt furnace-like in July.
items.exampleCN: 七月里阁楼热得像熔炉。

items.meaning: fuel oil for a heating furnace
items.example: They stored furnace oil in the cellar.
items.exampleCN: 他们把炉用燃油存放在地窖里。

items.meaning: a filter for a heating furnace
items.example: Change the furnace filter every month.
items.exampleCN: 每月更换一次暖气炉滤网。

items.example: He opened the furnace door carefully.

items.meaning: a room housing a heating furnace
items.example: The furnace room is in the basement.

latinEntries.example: The Latin fornax stands behind the English furnace.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 fornax 是英语 furnace 的来源。

definition_zh: 减去；去掉
definition_en: to take a number or amount away from another
core_image: 从一堆东西里拿走一部分，堆变小了
scene: 从十里面减去三，得到七。 Subtract three from ten and you get seven.
sceneCN: 这里 subtract 是「减去」（第 1 个义项）；句意：从十里面减去三，得到七。

senses.title: Take away
senses.definition: to take one number away from another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个数中减去另一个数
senses.example: Subtract three from ten and you get seven.
senses.exampleCN: 从十里面减去三，得到七。
senses.why: This is the basic arithmetic sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的算术义项。

senses.title: Deduct
senses.definition: to take an amount away from a total
senses.definitionCN: 从总数中扣除一笔数额
senses.example: Subtract the tax before you divide the profit.
senses.exampleCN: 分利润之前先扣除税款。
senses.why: Money follows the same arithmetic.
senses.whyCN: 钱的计算遵循同样的算术。

intro.en: Subtract joins Latin sub, away, with trahere, to pull.
intro.cn: subtract 由拉丁语 sub（离开）与 trahere（拉）组合而成。

items.en: Sub meant away or under.
items.cn: sub 意为离开或在下。

items.en: Trahere meant to pull or draw.
items.cn: trahere 意为拉、拖。

items.en: Subtrahere meant to pull away.
items.cn: subtrahere 意为拉走。

items.en: Subtract named the arithmetic operation.
items.cn: subtract 指算术中的减法。

items.en: Subtract widened to mean deduct money.
items.cn: subtract 扩展为扣除钱款。

note.en: Subtract is compared with look-alike words and with words for taking away.
note.cn: 把 subtract 与形近词以及表示拿走的词作比较。

entries.definition: to reduce the value of something

normalIntro.en: Subtract pulls a number away from the pile.
normalIntro.cn: subtract 就是把一个数从那一堆里拉走。

normal.en: Subtract three from ten and you get seven.
normal.cn: 从十里面减去三，得到七。

normal.en: Subtract the tax before you divide the profit.
normal.cn: 分利润之前先扣除税款。

normal.en: She can subtract quickly in her head.
normal.cn: 她心算减法很快。

normal.en: Subtract the cost from the total.
normal.cn: 从总额里扣除成本。

normal.en: Do not subtract the discount twice.
normal.cn: 不要把折扣扣两次。

abstract.en: We subtract years but not memories.
abstract.cn: 我们会减去年岁，却减不掉记忆。

abstract.en: Every subtraction leaves a smaller, truer number.
abstract.cn: 每一次减法，都留下一个更小却更真实的数。

abstract.en: To subtract is to decide what is not needed.
abstract.cn: 做减法，就是决定什么不需要。

examples.en: Subtract three from ten and you get seven.
examples.cn: 从十里面减去三，得到七。

examples.en: Subtract the tax before you divide the profit.
examples.cn: 分利润之前先扣除税款。

examples.en: Subtract the cost from the total.
examples.cn: 从总额里扣除成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: subtract 是「减去、扣除」；subtract from 是从……中减去，subtract the cost 是扣除成本，subtraction 是减法，加减乘除里的减就是它。

root: 来自拉丁语 subtrahere（拉走）的过去分词 subtractus，由 sub（离开）与 trahere（拉）组合；字面是「从里面拉走」，因此表示减去、扣除。

sensesIntro.en: Subtract means to take a number away, or to deduct an amount.
sensesIntro.cn: subtract 表示减去一个数，或扣除一笔数额。

core.en: A hand pulling part of a pile away.
core.cn: 一只手从堆里拉走一部分。

branches.en: Subtract three from ten and you get seven.
branches.cn: 从十里面减去三，得到七。

branches.en: Subtract the tax before you divide the profit.
branches.cn: 分利润之前先扣除税款。

branches.en: Arithmetic and money both take an amount away.
branches.cn: 算术和钱款，都是从总量中拿走一部分。

branches.en: She can subtract quickly in her head.
branches.cn: 她心算减法很快。

branches.en: Subtract the cost from the total.
branches.cn: 从总额里扣除成本。

intro.en: Subtract takes -ion and -ive to build its family.
intro.cn: subtract 借助 -ion 和 -ive 构成同族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base tract- meant pulled.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 tract- 意为拉。

items.exampleCN: 这是一个做减法的过程。

items.example: In ten minus three, three is the subtrahend.
Subtract the discount from the price.

latinEntries.example: Trahere gave English subtract and extract.
latinEntries.exampleCN: trahere 演变为英语的 subtract 和 extract。

definition_zh: 禁止；阻止；使不可能；（法律）禁止某人做某事
definition_en: to forbid something by law or rule, or to make it impossible
core_image: 一只手横在门前，掌心朝外，把来人挡回去
scene: 博物馆入口挂着一块牌子。 The sign at the entrance says that the rules prohibit flash photography, and the guard raises a hand whenever a camera comes up.
sceneCN: 这里 prohibit 是「禁止」（第 1 个义项：以规则明令不许做某事）；句意：入口的牌子写着规定禁止使用闪光灯，保安一看到有人举相机就抬手示意。图中可辨识物件：禁止标识、相机、闪光灯、保安的手、展厅入口；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 禁止的；（价格）高得使人却步的

senses.title: Forbid by law or rule
senses.definition: to state officially that something must not be done
senses.definitionCN: 官方规定某事不得做
senses.example: The law prohibits smoking indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 法律禁止室内吸烟。
senses.why: Latin prohibere means 'hold back'. The prefix pro- pushes away, and habere holds: the rule puts a hand out and holds the thing back from happening.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 prohibere 意为“挡住”。前缀 pro- 向外推，habere 是持握：规则伸出一只手，把此事挡在外面。

senses.title: Prevent or make impossible
senses.definition: to make something impossible in practice
senses.definitionCN: 使某事在实践中不可能
senses.example: The high cost prohibits most families from buying.
senses.exampleCN: 高昂的成本使多数家庭无法购买。
senses.why: The same holding-back can be economic rather than legal: price acts like a gate. Prohibitive costs prohibit without any statute.
senses.whyCN: 同一种“挡住”可以是经济的而非法律的：价格像一道门。 prohibitive 的成本无需法规就禁止了购买。

senses.title: Forbid a person from doing
senses.definition: to bar a specific person from an action
senses.definitionCN: 禁止特定的人采取某行动
senses.example: The court prohibited him from contacting her.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭禁止他联系她。
senses.why: When the object is a person, the rule targets an agent rather than an act. The structure prohibit someone from doing marks the boundary drawn around that person.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是人时，规则瞄准行动者而非行为本身。prohibit someone from doing 的结构，标记围绕此人画下的边界。

senses.title: An official ban
senses.definition: to ban something officially, often by authority
senses.definitionCN: 由权威正式取缔某物
senses.example: The city prohibited the sale of fireworks.
senses.exampleCN: 该市禁止销售烟花爆竹。
senses.why: A ban is the institutional form of the hand at the door. Prohibition is the noun, and it can name a whole historical policy, as in the American Prohibition.
senses.whyCN: 禁令是“门口那只手”的制度形式。prohibition 是名词，可以命名一整段历史政策，如美国禁酒令。

senses.title: Of a sign or notice: forbid entry or use
senses.definition: of a sign or instruction, to forbid an action or access
senses.definitionCN: 标识或指示禁止某行为或进入
senses.example: The sign prohibits entry without a badge.
senses.exampleCN: 标牌禁止无证进入。
senses.why: Public space is regulated by visible marks. The verb turns a printed symbol into a rule, and the sign becomes the hand made permanent.
senses.whyCN: 公共空间由可见标记管理。动词把印刷符号变成规则，标牌成了被永久化的那只手。

senses.title: Hinder or prevent (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to hinder or stand in the way of
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：妨碍或挡路
senses.example: Bad weather prohibited our advance.
senses.exampleCN: 恶劣天气阻碍了我们前进。
senses.why: This is the broadest layer: anything that holds you back prohibits you. Modern English narrows the word to rules and practical impossibility.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽的一层：任何挡住你的东西都 prohibit 你。现代英语把这个词收窄到规则与实际不可能。

senses.title: Restrain by legal writ
senses.definition: in law, to restrain an action by authority
senses.definitionCN: 法律中以权威限制某行为
senses.example: The injunction prohibits further construction.
senses.exampleCN: 禁令限制继续施工。
senses.why: Courts issue orders that function as verbal gates. The legal sense specializes the holding-back into a formal instrument with penalties attached.
senses.whyCN: 法院发布命令，功能如同语言的门。法律义把“挡住”专门化为附有惩罚的正式工具。

senses.title: Forbid access
senses.definition: to bar entry to a place
senses.definitionCN: 不许进入某地
senses.example: The area is prohibited to civilians.
senses.exampleCN: 该区域禁止平民进入。
senses.why: Access control is the most physical version: a fence, a guard, a sign. The verb names the rule that the barrier enforces.
senses.whyCN: 出入控制是最物理的版本：围栏、警卫、标牌。动词命名屏障所执行的规则。

intro.en: Prohibit is a holding-back word. Latin prohibere joins pro- 'away' to habere 'hold': to hold something away from you, and therefore to forbid it.
intro.cn: prohibit 是一个“挡住”的词。拉丁语 prohibere 把 pro-“向外”与 habere“持握”结合：把某物挡在你之外，因此就是禁止它。

items.en: First recorded as 'forbid, prevent', borrowed from Latin prohibitus.
items.cn: 最早记录为“禁止、阻止”，借自拉丁语 prohibitus。

items.en: prohibitus is the past participle of prohibere 'hold back, keep off, prevent, forbid' = pro- 'away, forth' + habere 'to hold'.
items.cn: prohibitus 是 prohibere 的过去分词，后者意为“挡住、隔开、阻止、禁止”= pro-“向外”+ habere“持握”。

items.en: habere also gives habit, exhibit, inhibit, and ability. The family is about holding, and pro- turns holding into holding away.
items.cn: habere 还生成 habit、exhibit、inhibit、ability。这个词族关乎持握，而 pro- 把“持握”变成“挡开”。

items.en: The noun prohibition and the adjective prohibitive develop, the latter also taking the sense 'so costly as to prevent'.
items.cn: 名词 prohibition 与形容词 prohibitive 发展出来，后者还取得“贵到使人却步”的义。

items.en: Modern English uses prohibit for legal bans, signs, and practical impossibility, keeping the image of a hand held out.
items.cn: 现代英语用 prohibit 指法律禁令、标识与实际不可能，保留“伸出手挡住”的意象。

note.en: The first group shares the habere root; the second is about verbs that also mean forbidding or preventing.
note.cn: 第一组共享 habere 词根，第二组看同样表示“禁止”或“阻止”的动词。

entries.definition: to restrain or slow down. It uses in- 'in' + habere, holding in.
entries.definitionCN: 抑制；阻碍。它用 in-“在内”+ habere，持握在内。

entries.definition: to show publicly. It is ex- 'out' + habere, holding out.
entries.definitionCN: 公开展示。它是 ex-“向外”+ habere，持出在外。

entries.definition: an official ban, or the historical US ban on alcohol.
to order someone not to do something. It is broader and more personal than prohibit.
entries.definitionCN: 命令某人不要做。它比 prohibit 更宽、更对人。

entries.definition: to forbid something officially, often by public authority. It is the plain word behind prohibition.
entries.definitionCN: 官方禁止，常由公共权威发布。它是 prohibition 背后的平实词。

entries.definition: to stop something from happening. It covers both rules and practical obstacles.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某事发生。它涵盖规则与实际障碍。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin habere 'hold' with pro- 'away', the inhibit/exhibit family, the sign use, and prohibitive cost.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 habere“持握”加 pro-“向外”、inhibit/exhibit 词族、标识用法，以及 prohibitive cost。

normal.en: Habere means 'hold'; pro- means 'away'. Prohibit is to hold something away from you: a hand at the door.
normal.cn: habere 意为“持握”；pro- 意为“向外”。prohibit 就是把东西挡在你之外：门口的一只手。

normal.en: Inhibit holds in, exhibit holds out, prohibit holds away: the prefix tells you the direction.
normal.cn: inhibit 向内持，exhibit 向外持，prohibit 挡开：前缀告诉你方向。

normal.en: A prohibition sign is the hand made permanent: the rule stays at the door even when no guard is there.
normal.cn: 禁止标识是被永久化的那只手：即使没有警卫，规则仍守在门口。

normal.en: Prohibitive costs prohibit without a law: price acts as a gate.
normal.cn: prohibitive 的成本无需法律就禁止：价格就是门。

normal.en: The word targets both acts and people: you prohibit smoking, and you prohibit someone from smoking.
normal.cn: 这个词既针对行为也针对人：prohibit smoking，也 prohibit someone from smoking。

abstract.en: Every prohibition draws a boundary, and every boundary creates a category of the forbidden.
abstract.cn: 每一项禁令都画出一条边界，每条边界都造出“被禁止者”这一类别。

abstract.en: Forbidding is cheaper than preventing: a rule costs words, a wall costs stone.
abstract.cn: 禁止比阻止便宜：规则花的是话，墙花的是石头。

abstract.en: The same verb covers law and economics, which shows that constraint has many currencies.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词覆盖法律与经济，说明约束有多种货币。

examples.en: Smoking is prohibited in all public buildings.
examples.cn: 所有公共建筑内禁止吸烟。

examples.en: The high price prohibits many students from applying.
examples.cn: 高昂的价格使许多学生无法申请。

examples.en: The court prohibited the company from selling the drug.
examples.cn: 法庭禁止该公司销售这种药物。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若黑壁”——扑到黑色的墙壁前被挡住 → prohibit 禁止、阻止

root: 拉丁语 prohibere“挡住、禁止”= pro-“向外”+ habere“持握”；同族有 habit、exhibit、inhibit、ability。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of prohibit, all one gesture: holding something away. The hand can be a law, a sign, a court order, a price, or a fence.
sensesIntro.cn: prohibit 的八个义项，都是同一个手势：把某物挡在外面。这只手可以是法律、标识、法院命令、价格或围栏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held out to keep something away.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸出一只手，把某物挡在外面。

branches.en: RULE: laws, bans, and signs state what must not be done.
branches.cn: 规则：法律、禁令与标识规定什么不得做。

branches.en: PERSON AND COURT: an order can be drawn around a specific person or action.
branches.cn: 人与法庭：命令可围绕特定人或行为画界。

branches.en: ACCESS: a barrier enforces the rule at a physical threshold.
branches.cn: 进入：屏障在物理门槛上执行规则。

branches.en: ECONOMICS: price holds people back without any statute.
branches.cn: 经济：价格无需法规就把人挡住。

branches.en: HINDRANCE: the archaic sense covers any obstacle that holds you back.
branches.cn: 妨碍：古义涵盖任何挡住你的障碍。

intro.en: Prohibit is a Latin verb. English adds -ion, -ive, and -ed, and the root habere also builds inhibit, exhibit, and habit.
intro.cn: prohibit 是拉丁动词。英语加 -ion、-ive、-ed，词根 habere 还构成 inhibit、exhibit、habit。

latinIntro.en: Latin prohibere 'hold back' combines pro- 'away' with habere 'hold'. The same habere underlies exhibit (hold out), inhibit (hold in), and habit (what one holds).
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prohibere“挡住”把 pro-“向外”与 habere“持握”结合。同一个 habere 支撑 exhibit（持出）、inhibit（持内）与 habit（所持之物）。

items.meaning: an official ban; the act of forbidding
forbidding; so costly as to prevent use
items.meaningCN: 禁止性的；贵得使人却步的

items.meaning: a settled practice; a customary way

latinEntries.meaning: to hold back, keep off, forbid

definition_zh: 锚；使固定；新闻主播；（精神上的）支柱
definition_en: a heavy device dropped from a boat to hold it in place, the act of fixing something firmly, or a person who presents the news
core_image: 一只铁锚沉入海底，缆绳绷紧，船停住了
scene: 风浪里，船长把船开到海湾，抛下锚等天亮。 They anchored the boat in the bay until the storm passed.
sceneCN: 这里 anchor 是「抛锚；使固定」（第 2 个义项：作动词，用锚把船固定住）；句意是他们把船停在湾里抛锚，直到风暴过去。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：未固定的；无依无靠的

senses.title: The device that holds a ship
senses.definition: a heavy metal object dropped from a ship so that its weight and grip on the seabed hold the ship in place
senses.definitionCN: 从船上沉入水底的重金属物，凭重量与抓力把船固定在原处
senses.example: The ship let down its anchor outside the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 船在港口外抛下了锚。
senses.why: The word came into English from Greek and Latin names for the same iron hook, so the object has kept its name for more than a thousand years.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经由希腊语与拉丁语中指同一铁钩的名称进入英语，所以这个物件一千多年来都叫同一个名字。

senses.title: To fix something in place
senses.definition: to hold a boat or an object firmly in one position
senses.definitionCN: 把船或物体牢牢固定在某个位置
senses.example: They anchored the boat in the bay until the storm passed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把船停在海湾里抛锚，直到风暴过去。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb because anchoring is an action, and from boats the verb spread to any object fixed firmly to the ground.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，是因为「抛锚」是一个动作；从船只开始，这个动词扩展到任何被牢牢固定在地面的物体。

senses.title: A mainstay or news presenter
senses.definition: a person who gives stability to a group or programme, especially the presenter who holds a news broadcast together
senses.definitionCN: 给团体或节目提供稳定性的人，尤指串联整档新闻的主播
senses.example: She has been the anchor of the evening news for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 她主持晚间新闻已经十年了。
senses.why: A news anchor holds a programme in place the way an anchor holds a ship, and the same metaphor extends to a family's steady centre.
senses.whyCN: 新闻主播稳住一档节目，就像锚稳住一艘船；同样的比喻也延伸到家庭中那个稳定的中心人物。

intro.en: Anchor is an ancient sea word, borrowed from Greek through Latin and into Old English.
intro.cn: anchor 是古老的航海词，经拉丁语从希腊语借入古英语。

items.en: ankyra meant 'anchor', and it is also the source of the medical word ankylosis.
items.cn: ankyra 意为「锚」，也是医学术语 ankylosis 的来源。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as ancora, the term used by sailors.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 ancora，是水手使用的说法。

items.en: Old English took the word from Latin and used it for the iron hook.
items.cn: 古英语从拉丁语借入 ancor，指铁锚。

items.en: The spelling shifted towards anchor under Latin influence.
items.cn: 在拉丁语影响下，拼写逐渐变为 anchor。

items.en: The figurative senses grew in broadcasting and in everyday talk about stability.
items.cn: 比喻义在广播行业与日常谈「稳定」时发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sea root; the near-meaning group gives mooring and support words.
note.cn: 形近组共享航海词根；近义组给出停泊与支撑类词。

entries.definition: a place where ships may anchor
to tie a boat to the shore

normalIntro.en: An anchor holds a ship the way a mainstay holds a family.
normalIntro.cn: 锚稳住船，就像支柱稳住家庭。

normal.en: Drop anchor to stop, weigh anchor to leave.
normal.cn: drop anchor 是抛锚停下，weigh anchor 是起锚离开。

normal.en: The news anchor holds the programme together.
normal.cn: 新闻主播把整档节目串联起来。

normal.en: Anchor is both a noun and a verb.
normal.cn: anchor 既是名词也是动词。

normal.en: Greek ankyra is the oldest form we can trace.
normal.cn: 可追溯的最早形式是希腊语 ankyra。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-chor.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-chor。

abstract.en: Picture an iron hook biting into the seabed.
abstract.cn: 想象铁钩咬进海底。

abstract.en: See a taut rope and a still boat.
abstract.cn: 想象绷紧的缆绳与停稳的船。

abstract.en: Imagine a presenter holding a broadcast steady.
abstract.cn: 想象主播稳住一整档直播。

examples.en: They dropped anchor just outside the reef.
examples.cn: 他们就在礁石外抛了锚。

examples.en: The tent was anchored to the ground with strong ropes.
examples.cn: 帐篷用粗绳固定在地上。

examples.en: He became the anchor of the morning news programme.
examples.cn: 他成了早间新闻节目的主播。

dict_mnemonic.text: anchor 听起来像「安可」：把船安好、可停稳，靠的就是锚。

root: 源自希腊语 ankyra「锚」，经拉丁语 ancora 与古英语 ancor 进入英语，拼写在拉丁语影响下变为 anchor；由实物的锚引申出「固定」的动词义，以及新闻主播、家庭支柱等比喻义。

sensesIntro.en: One iron hook gives three uses: the object, the act of fixing, and the person who steadies things.
sensesIntro.cn: 一只铁锚生出三种用法：物件本身、固定的动作，以及稳住局面的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an iron hook biting into the seabed.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁钩咬住海底。

branches.en: dropping anchor outside a harbour
branches.cn: 在港外抛锚

branches.en: weighing anchor at dawn
branches.cn: 黎明起锚

branches.en: a tent roped to the ground
branches.cn: 用绳固定的帐篷

branches.en: a boat held through a storm
branches.cn: 风暴中固定住的船

branches.en: the anchor of the evening news
branches.cn: 晚间新闻主播

intro.en: A Greek sea word with a small English family and a strong figurative life.
intro.cn: 这是希腊航海词，英语中有一小族词，比喻用法也很活跃。

latinIntro.en: Latin ancora is the bridge between Greek and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ancora 是希腊语与英语之间的桥梁。

items.meaning: a device to hold a ship

items.example: an anchor point for the rope

definition_zh: 选举产生的；有选举权的；选修的；选修课；择期的
definition_en: filled by election, having the right to vote, chosen rather than required, a course freely chosen, or scheduled rather than urgent
core_image: 课表上最后一栏空着，学生自己填上一门课
scene: 课表最后一栏留白，她在两门课之间挑了陶艺。 Students may take one elective in their final year.
sceneCN: 这里 elective 是「选修课」（第 4 个义项：由学生自由选择而非必修的课程）；句意是学生在最后一年可以修一门选修课。

pos.zh: 形容词：选举产生的；有选举权的；选修的；择期的

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉形容词后缀 -ive 得到，义为「选举；选择」
由 elect 加 -ion 构成，义为「选举」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「选修地；可选择地」

senses.title: Filled by election
senses.definition: of a post or body, filled or decided by voting rather than by appointment
senses.definitionCN: 指职位或机构，由投票产生而非任命
senses.example: The mayor holds an elective office.
senses.exampleCN: 市长这一职位是民选的。
senses.why: Elective is elect plus -ive: the post has the property of being filled by a picking out.
senses.whyCN: elective 是 elect 加 -ive：这个职位带有「靠挑出来填补」的性质。

senses.title: Chosen rather than required
senses.definition: of a course or subject, taken by choice and not required
senses.definitionCN: 指课程或科目，出于自愿而非必修
senses.example: Music is an elective subject at this school.
senses.exampleCN: 在这所学校，音乐是选修科目。
senses.why: A student picking a course repeats the same picking out, so the word moves from offices to classrooms.
senses.whyCN: 学生挑一门课重复的是同一种「挑出」，于是这个词从职位走到了教室。

senses.title: Having the right to vote
senses.definition: of a person or body, possessing the right to vote in elections
senses.definitionCN: 指人或机构，拥有在选举中投票的权利
senses.example: The upper house is partly elective and partly appointed.
senses.exampleCN: 上议院部分由选举产生，部分由任命产生。
senses.why: The right to do the picking is itself described by the same adjective, so elective also means entitled to vote.
senses.whyCN: 做这次「挑出」的权利也用同一个形容词描述，所以 elective 也指「有选举权」。

senses.title: A course freely chosen
senses.definition: a course that a student chooses to take rather than one required by the programme
senses.definitionCN: 学生自愿选择而非培养方案规定的课程
senses.example: Students may take one elective in their final year.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在最后一年可以修一门选修课。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the thing chosen, the way a quality becomes an object.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成「被选中之物」的名词，就像一种性质变成了实物。

senses.title: Scheduled rather than urgent
senses.definition: of medical treatment, planned in advance rather than needed at once
senses.definitionCN: 指医疗处置，事先安排而非当下必须进行
senses.example: The operation was elective, so it could wait a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这台手术是择期的，所以可以等一个月。
senses.why: What can be chosen in time is what is not forced by emergency, so elective also marks the optional in medicine.
senses.whyCN: 能在时间上挑选的，就是不被急症逼迫的，所以 elective 在医学里也标出「可选择」的部分。

intro.en: Elective is Latin electivus, from eligere, to pick out, with the adjective ending -ivus; English uses it for posts, courses and treatments.
intro.cn: elective 是拉丁语 electivus，由 eligere（挑出）加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成；英语把它用于职位、课程与医疗。

items.en: Legere meant to pick or gather, the base of the family.
items.cn: legere 意为「挑选、收集」，是整个词族的词基。

items.en: E- out plus legere formed the verb to pick out.
items.cn: e-（出）加 legere 构成「挑出」的动词。

items.en: The adjective described something that operates by choice or election.
items.cn: 这个形容词描述靠选择或选举来运作的事物。

items.en: Church and university Latin applied it to offices that were filled by voting.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把它用于靠投票填补的职位。

items.en: English added the school sense of a chosen course and the medical sense of planned treatment.
items.cn: 英语又加入「自选课程」与「择期治疗」两个义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elect family; the near-meaning group separates optional, voluntary and selective.
note.cn: 形近组收 elect 词族；近义组区分 optional、voluntary 与 selective。

entries.definition: To choose a person for a post by voting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「选举」，是本词的词基。

entries.definition: The process of choosing by vote.
A person with the right to vote.
Not required; it can be left out entirely, which elective courses cannot.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可选的」，可以完全不做，而选修课仍需修满学分。

entries.definition: Done by free will, often without pay or pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自愿的」，强调出于自由意志。

entries.definition: Careful about what is chosen, or affecting only some; from the same root but a different idea.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有选择的、严格挑选的」，同根而义不同。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a blank slot on a timetable, then widen to an elected post and a planned operation.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从课表上的一个空格出发，再扩到民选职位与择期手术。

normal.en: Elective is elect plus -ive: something filled or taken by choosing.
normal.cn: elective 是 elect 加 -ive：靠挑选来填补或取得的东西。

normal.en: An elective office is one you have to be voted into.
normal.cn: elective office 是必须靠投票才能坐上的职位。

normal.en: An elective course is a blank on the timetable you fill yourself.
normal.cn: elective course 是课表上由你自己填的空格。

normal.en: The noun elective means the course, not the choosing.
normal.cn: 名词 elective 指那门课，而不是选择这个动作。

normal.en: Elective surgery can wait; emergency surgery cannot.
normal.cn: 择期手术可以等，急诊手术不能等。

abstract.en: Picture a form with one line left empty on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格，有一行被故意留空。

abstract.en: The same empty line can be a seat to be voted on, a course, or a date for surgery.
abstract.cn: 同一个空格可以是要投票的席位、一门课，或一个手术日期。

abstract.en: Elective marks whatever is left open to choice.
abstract.cn: elective 标记的是一切仍向选择敞开的东西。

examples.en: The mayor holds an elective office.
examples.cn: 市长这一职位是民选的。

examples.en: Music is an elective subject at this school.
examples.cn: 在这所学校，音乐是选修科目。

examples.en: Students may take one elective in their final year.
examples.cn: 学生在最后一年可以修一门选修课。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊莱克提夫」——课表上留了一格，自己填一门课

root: 拉丁语 eligere「挑出」加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成 electivus，义为「靠选择或选举运作的」；英语据此发展出民选、选修、择期诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of elective: filled by vote, chosen rather than required, entitled to vote, a chosen course, and planned rather than urgent.
sensesIntro.cn: elective 的五个义项：民选的、选修的、有选举权的、选修课，以及择期而非紧急的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blank line on a timetable that a student fills in.
core.cn: 核心意象：课表上一条由学生自己填的空行。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a seat that only votes can fill.
branches.cn: 职位线：只有投票才能填上的席位。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: a course taken by preference.
branches.cn: 科目线：凭偏好选上的科目。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: the power to take part in the picking.
branches.cn: 权利线：参与这次挑选的权力。

branches.en: THE COURSE: the adjective becomes the thing chosen.
branches.cn: 课程线：形容词变成被选中之物。

branches.en: THE OPTIONAL: study and treatment both moved to a date of your choosing.
branches.cn: 可选线：学业与治疗都被挪到你挑选的时间。

intro.en: Elective is the Latin -ivus adjective of eligere; English adds -ly and keeps the same stem for elect and election.
intro.cn: elective 是 eligere 的拉丁语 -ivus 形容词；英语再加 -ly，并与 elect、election 共用同一词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin electivus is recorded, and its base verbs are attested, so only the oldest root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 electivus 有记录，其词基动词也有书证，只有最古老的词根属于重构。

items.example: It is the direct source adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是直接的来源形容词。

definition_zh: 微湿的；湿润的；潮湿的；（食物）湿润柔软的
definition_en: slightly wet, especially in a soft or pleasant way rather than soaked
core_image: 刚拧过的毛巾还留着水痕，摸上去凉而柔，却不会滴下水来
scene: 面包师把一块微湿的布盖在面团上，布面只是潮潮的。 The baker laid a moist cloth over the dough.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「带少量水、微湿而不滴水」（第 1 个义项：表面轻微湿润）；句意为面包师把一块微湿的布盖在面团上；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 微湿的；湿润的；（气候）潮湿的；（食物）湿润柔软的

senses.title: Slightly wet to the touch
senses.definition: slightly wet, with enough water to be felt but not enough to drip
senses.definitionCN: 带有一点可被摸出的水，但还不到往下滴的程度
senses.example: The baker laid a moist cloth over the dough.
senses.exampleCN: 面包师把一块微湿的布盖在面团上。
senses.why: Moist is the adjective of the moisture family, so it describes the state of holding a small amount of water, never being soaked.
senses.whyCN: moist 是 moisture 词族的形容词，描述「持有少量水」的状态，而不是被水浸透。

senses.title: Soil that holds water for roots
senses.titleCN: 能保住水供根系吸收的土壤
senses.definition: soil that is damp enough for plants to draw water from it
senses.definitionCN: 湿润到足以让植物从其中吸水生长的土壤
senses.example: Seedlings grow fastest in moist soil.
senses.exampleCN: 幼苗在湿润的土壤里长得最快。
senses.why: A surface that holds the right amount of water is good ground; the same adjective follows the water into the earth.
senses.whyCN: 恰好留住适量水的表面就是好土地；同一个形容词跟着水走进了泥土。

senses.title: Air carrying water vapour
senses.definition: air that contains noticeable water vapour, often warm and heavy
senses.definitionCN: 含有明显水汽、常显得温暖沉闷的空气
senses.example: A moist wind blew in from the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵潮湿的风从海上吹来。
senses.why: Air can be wet without being liquid, so moist here describes what the air holds rather than what it touches.
senses.whyCN: 空气可以非液态地「湿」着，所以这里的 moist 描述空气所含之物，而不是它碰到的东西。

senses.title: Food with a soft, wet texture
senses.definition: food that is soft and retains water, usually said with approval
senses.definitionCN: 柔软并保住了水的食物，通常带赞许意味
senses.example: The cake stays moist for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 这块蛋糕能保持湿润三天。
senses.why: For bakers, dryness is the fault and moisture the virtue, so moist became a word of praise on a menu.
senses.whyCN: 对烘焙者来说，干是缺点、湿是优点，于是 moist 成了菜单上的褒词。

senses.title: Eyes filled with tears
senses.definition: eyes that are wet because tears are rising in them
senses.definitionCN: 因泪水涌起而显得湿的眼睛
senses.example: Her eyes grew moist when the letter was read aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 信被大声念出来时，她的眼睛湿了。
senses.why: The body's own water shows an inner state; the adjective moves from weather and food to feeling.
senses.whyCN: 身体里的水显露内心状态，这个形容词于是从天气与食物走到了情感。

senses.title: A damp climate or season
senses.definition: a climate or season with persistently damp air
senses.definitionCN: 空气长期潮湿的气候或季节
senses.example: The valley has a moist climate that suits ferns.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷气候潮湿，很适合蕨类生长。
senses.why: When dampness lasts long enough to define a place, the word becomes a description of climate.
senses.whyCN: 当潮湿持续得足以定义一个地方时，这个词就成了对气候的描述。

senses.title: Tissue kept from drying out
senses.definition: in medicine and skin care, tissue kept in its natural damp state
senses.definitionCN: 医学与护肤语境中，保持在天然湿润状态的组织
senses.example: Keep the wound moist while it heals.
senses.exampleCN: 伤口愈合期间要保持湿润。
senses.why: Medical writers borrowed the plain adjective to mean 'not allowed to dry', the same idea applied to a patient.
senses.whyCN: 医学写作借用了这个普通形容词，表示「不让变干」，只是把同一想法用到病人身上。

senses.title: Moist heat in cooking and therapy
senses.definition: heat carried by steam or water rather than by dry air
senses.definitionCN: 由蒸汽或水而非干热空气传导的热
senses.example: Braising cooks the meat with moist heat.
senses.exampleCN: 炖煮用湿热把肉做熟。
senses.why: Here moist does not describe an object but a medium: heat that travels with water.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 moist 不描述物体，而描述介质：随水一起传导的热。

intro.en: Moist comes from Old French and its Latin background is contested. The reconstruction is labelled as a hypothesis; the word's deeper source is marked as source uncertain.
intro.cn: moist 来自古法语，其拉丁背景存在争议。重构形式已标注为假说；更深来源不确定。

items.en: Old French moiste meant 'wet, damp, fresh', and also 'newly made, still soft', a range wider than the modern English word.
items.cn: 古法语 moiste 意为「湿的、潮湿的、新鲜的」，也有「刚做成、仍柔软的」义，范围比现代英语更宽。

items.en: English took moiste as moist and used it for damp air, damp earth and food that had not dried out.
items.cn: 英语借入为 moist，用于潮湿的空气、湿润的土地和没有变干的食物。

items.en: The common reconstruction is Vulgar Latin *muscidus 'mouldy', an altered form of Latin mucidus. The alteration is assumed, not attested.
items.cn: 常见重构是俗拉丁语 *muscidus「发霉的」，为拉丁语 mucidus 的变形。这一变形是假定，并无文献记录。

items.en: Other scholars link the Romance family to Latin madidus 'wet, soaked' and madere 'to be wet'. The two hypotheses are usually presented together rather than decided.
items.cn: 另一些学者把这一罗曼语词族联系到拉丁语 madidus「湿透的」与 madere「潮湿」。两种假说通常并列陈述，不作定论。

items.en: The 'eyes wet with tears' use appears in the sixteenth century, and the approving culinary use became common in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 「眼睛含泪」的用法出现于十六世纪，带赞许意味的烹饪用法在十九世纪变得常见。

note.en: Group one holds short words that look or sound close to moist; group two holds adjectives that also describe water.
note.cn: 第一组是与 moist 字形或读音接近的短词；第二组是也描述水分的形容词。

entries.definition: The superlative of much or many. It has a long vowel and ends in -st, and comes from Old English mǣst, not from the moist family.
entries.definitionCN: much 或 many 的最高级。元音较长，词尾是 -st，源自古英语 mǣst，与 moist 词族无关。

entries.definition: To lift something with ropes or a machine. The vowel is /ɔɪ/ and the first consonant is h-, so the two words are not related.
entries.definitionCN: 用绳索或机械把某物升起。元音是 /ɔɪ/，首辅音是 h-，两词没有词源关系。

entries.definition: A modal verb of obligation, or the juice of crushed grapes. The vowel is /ʌ/ and the meaning has nothing to do with dampness.
entries.definitionCN: 表示义务的情态动词，或压碎的葡萄汁。元音是 /ʌ/，意义与潮湿无关。

entries.definition: Slightly wet, usually in a way that feels cold or unpleasant; damp often criticises where moist may praise.
entries.definitionCN: 微湿，通常带阴冷或不适感；damp 常带批评，而 moist 可能带赞许。

entries.definition: Describing air or weather that holds a lot of water vapour, usually oppressively so; it applies to air, rarely to cake.
entries.definitionCN: 形容空气或天气含水汽多，常令人闷热；它用于空气，很少用于蛋糕。

entries.definition: Covered or soaked with liquid water; it is stronger than moist and implies visible water or a thorough soaking.
entries.definitionCN: 被液态水覆盖或浸透；比 moist 更强，暗示可见的水或彻底浸湿。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes and real compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：使用真实的后缀与真实的复合词，不编造顺口溜。

normal.en: moist is the adjective, moisture is the noun: remove the -ure noun ending and you are left with the describing word.
normal.cn: moist 是形容词，moisture 是名词：去掉名词后缀 -ure，就剩下那个描述性的词。

normal.en: moisten adds -en 'make', the same pattern as deepen and strengthen, so it means 'make moist'.
normal.cn: moisten 加 -en「使……」，与 deepen、strengthen 同构，所以就是「使湿润」。

normal.en: moistness is moist plus -ness, the standard suffix for a quality, as in kindness and darkness.
normal.cn: moistness 是 moist 加 -ness，这是表示性质的标准后缀，如 kindness、darkness。

normal.en: moist heat is a real cooking term opposed to dry heat: braising and steaming use steam, roasting and grilling use dry air.
normal.cn: moist heat 是真实的烹饪术语，与 dry heat 相对：炖、蒸用蒸汽，烤、炙用干热空气。

normal.en: moist eyes is a common written phrase for tears about to fall, linking a physical film of water to emotion.
normal.cn: moist eyes 是常见的书面搭配，指快要落下的眼泪，把一层水的物理薄膜与情绪连在一起。

abstract.en: Abstractly, moist is water below the dripping point: enough to be felt, not enough to fall. Symbol: a towel that leaves a print on the table but no puddle.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，moist 是还没到滴落点的水：足以被感觉到，却不足以落下来。符号：一条在桌上留下印子却没有积水的毛巾。

abstract.en: The same 'just enough water' can be praise in a cake, a warning in a wall, and tenderness in an eye.
abstract.cn: 同样的「恰好够的水」，在蛋糕里是赞美，在墙里是警告，在眼睛里是柔情。

abstract.en: So moist never means soaked; it always means a small, contained, often welcome amount.
abstract.cn: 所以 moist 从不表示浸透，而总是表示少量、被收住、往往还是受欢迎的一份水。

examples.en: Turn the soil while it is still moist but not muddy.
examples.cn: 趁土还湿润但没变成泥的时候翻土。

examples.en: A moist towel is better than a dry one for cleaning up dust.
examples.cn: 擦灰时用湿毛巾比干毛巾好用。

examples.en: The air felt moist before the storm arrived.
examples.cn: 暴风雨来临前，空气显得潮乎乎的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「抹湿」：抹布一抹，桌面就湿了 → moist 微湿的

root: 古法语 moiste「湿的」；其拉丁来源有争议，通常重构为俗拉丁语 *muscidus（源自拉丁 mucidus「发霉的」），也有学者联系 madere「潮湿」，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: water just below the dripping point. The word starts at a surface, then enters soil, air, food, eyes, climate, healing tissue and finally a cooking medium.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个意思展开：还没到滴落点的水。这个词从表面开始，随后进入土壤、空气、食物、眼睛、气候、愈合中的组织，最后成为一种烹饪介质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface that is cool and slightly dark with water but never drips.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块被水弄得发凉、颜色略深、却始终不滴水的表面。

branches.en: A FILM OF WATER: plain touch and medical care both describe tissue that holds a little water.
branches.cn: 一层水膜：日常触摸与医疗护理都在描述含着少量水的组织。

branches.en: DAMP MEDIA: soil and air hold water invisibly, one for roots and one as vapour.
branches.cn: 潮湿介质：土壤与空气都看不见地含水，一个为根系，一个以水汽。

branches.en: WATER AS A MEDIUM: in baking it keeps food soft; in cooking it carries heat as steam.
branches.cn: 水作介质：烘焙时它让食物柔软；烹饪时它以蒸汽搬运热量。

branches.en: EMOTION: tears rising make the eye itself the moist surface.
branches.cn: 情感：涌起的泪水让眼睛本身成了那块湿润的表面。

branches.en: PLACE: lasting dampness becomes a climate, no longer a passing sensation.
branches.cn: 地方：持久的潮湿变成一种气候，而不再是暂时的感觉。

intro.en: Moist is the base adjective of a productive family: -en makes a verb, -ness a quality noun, -ure a mass noun, and -ize builds the cosmetics verb.
intro.cn: moist 是一个能产词族的基础形容词：-en 造动词，-ness 造性质名词，-ure 造物质名词，-ize 造护肤动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin background of moist is disputed and cannot be stated safely, so the Latin entry list is empty on purpose. The related words below are all English formations or Old French borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: moist 的拉丁背景存在争议，无法稳妥陈述，因此拉丁词条列表按设计留空。下面的相关词都是英语构词或古法语借词。

items.meaningCN: 使微湿；沾湿（-en 表示「使……」）
items.example: Moisten the edge before sealing the envelope.
items.exampleCN: 封信封前先把边缘弄湿。

items.meaning: the state of being slightly wet
items.meaningCN: 湿润的状态（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The moistness of the air warned of rain.
items.exampleCN: 空气的湿润预示着要下雨。

items.meaningCN: 湿气；水分（-ure 构成物质名词）
items.example: The soil loses moisture in July.
items.exampleCN: 七月里土壤会失去水分。

items.meaning: to add water to skin or hair
items.meaningCN: 给皮肤或头发补水（-ize 构成动词）

items.meaning: a product used to add water to the skin
items.meaningCN: 保湿产品（-er 表示施动者）
items.example: She keeps a moisturizer in her bag.
items.exampleCN: 她包里常备一支保湿霜。

items.example: Store the salt in a moisture-proof jar.

items.meaning: heat carried by steam or water in cooking
items.meaningCN: 湿热（烹饪中由蒸汽或水传导的热）
items.exampleCN: 湿热做法能让肉保持嫩。

items.meaningCN: 眼含泪水的（moist 与 eyed 构成的复合形容词）
items.example: The audience sat moist-eyed at the end.
items.exampleCN: 结束时观众坐着，眼里含着泪。

definition_zh: 骑手；骑马的人；附加条款
definition_en: a person who rides a horse or bicycle, or an extra clause added to a document
core_image: 草原上勒住缰绳的骑手
scene: 草原上，骑手勒住缰绳让马慢慢停下。 The rider pulled the reins and slowed the horse.
sceneCN: 这里 rider 是「骑手」（第 1 个义项：骑马或骑车的人）；句意：草原上，骑手勒住缰绳让马慢慢停下。

pos.zh: 骑手；骑马的人；附加条款

senses.title: A person on horseback
senses.definition: a person who rides a horse
senses.definitionCN: 骑马的人
senses.example: The rider guided the horse across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 骑手引导马穿过田野。
senses.why: Ride plus -er names the person who rides.
senses.whyCN: ride 加 -er 就指进行骑乘的人。

senses.title: A person on a bike
senses.definition: a person who rides a bicycle or motorcycle
senses.definitionCN: 骑自行车或摩托车的人
senses.example: A rider in a yellow coat passed us.
senses.exampleCN: 一位穿黄外套的骑车人超过我们。
senses.why: The same -er word covers any vehicle you ride.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -er 后缀也涵盖任何可骑乘的交通工具。

senses.title: An extra clause
senses.definition: an additional condition added to a law or contract
senses.definitionCN: 附加在法律或合同上的额外条件
senses.example: They added a rider to protect the tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 他们增加了一条保护租客的附加条款。
senses.why: A rider travels along with the main document.
senses.whyCN: 附加条款跟随主文件一起同行。

intro.en: Rider is simply ride plus -er, the person who rides.
intro.cn: rider 就是 ride 加 -er，即进行骑乘的人。

items.en: Ridan means to ride.
items.cn: ridan 意为骑乘。

items.en: Ride keeps the old verb.
items.cn: ride 保留了这一古老动词。

items.en: -er marks the person who does it.
items.cn: -er 标记做这件事的人。

items.en: Rider also means an extra clause.
items.cn: rider 也指附加条款。

items.en: The legal sense grows from papers that ride along.
items.cn: 法律义来自随主文件同行的附加页。

note.en: A rider rides; a cyclist is the usual word for a bicycle rider.
note.cn: rider 指骑乘者；cyclist 是骑车人更常用的说法。

entries.definition: to sit on and control a horse or bike
a person who rides a bicycle
a person travelling in a vehicle

normalIntro.en: A rider is the rider on the ride.
normalIntro.cn: rider 就是骑在 ride 上的那个人。

normal.en: Add -er to ride to get rider.
normal.cn: ride 加 -er 就得到 rider。

normal.en: A horse rider holds the reins.
normal.cn: horse rider 握着缰绳。

normal.en: A bicycle rider wears a helmet.
normal.cn: bicycle rider 戴着头盔。

normal.en: A rider to a bill changes the law.
normal.cn: rider to a bill 会改变法律。

normal.en: A free rider pays nothing.
normal.cn: free rider 不付任何代价。

abstract.en: Picture a lone figure on a galloping horse.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孤独的身影骑在飞奔的马上。

abstract.en: Imagine a slip of paper riding along with a contract.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸片跟着合同一起旅行。

abstract.en: Think of a bike light moving through the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏车灯在黑暗中移动。

examples.en: The rider wore a red helmet.
examples.cn: 这位骑车人戴着红色头盔。

examples.en: Every rider must pay for the trip.
examples.cn: 每位乘车人都必须为行程付费。

examples.en: A rider was added to the agreement.
examples.cn: 协议中增加了一条附加条款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ride（骑）＋ r」——骑在马上的人，就是骑手。

root: ride（骑）＋ -er（人）→ rider，核心义「骑乘的人」；法律义由「随文件同行的附页」引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: A rider can be a person on a horse or bike, or an extra clause attached to a document.
sensesIntro.cn: rider 可以指骑马或骑车的人，也可以指附加在文件上的条款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure holding reins on a horse.
core.cn: 核心意象：握着缰绳骑在马上的人。

branches.en: The rider on a horse is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 骑马的人是这个词最古老的义项。

branches.en: The same person word now covers bikes.
branches.cn: 同一个表示人的词如今也涵盖自行车。

branches.en: A clause rides along with the main document.
branches.cn: 附加条款跟着主文件一起走。

branches.en: Both horse and bike riders sit and control.
branches.cn: 骑马与骑车的人都是坐着操控。

branches.en: The person sense and the paper sense share the idea of riding along.
branches.cn: 人义与文件义都共享「随行」的概念。

intro.en: Rider is ride plus the person suffix -er.
intro.cn: rider 是 ride 加表示人的后缀 -er。

latinIntro.en: The word stays close to its Old English verb ridan.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词一直贴近古英语动词 ridan。

items.example: -er turns a verb into a person.
items.exampleCN: -er 把动词变成表示人的名词。

items.example: Free rider adds a social sense.
items.exampleCN: free rider 增加了一层社会含义。

definition_zh: 游行；阅兵；炫耀；列队行进
definition_en: an organized public procession, a formal march of troops for inspection, a display meant to impress, and the act of marching in such a group
core_image: 彩旗在前，鼓点整齐，一条街被队伍填满
scene: 国庆那天的长街上，鼓乐队走在最前面，人群挤在两侧挥手。 The whole town turned out to watch the parade pass the old town hall.
sceneCN: 这里 parade 是「游行」（第 1 个义项：庆祝性的公众行进）；句意为全城人都出来看队伍经过旧市政厅。图中可辨识物件：彩旗、鼓、街道两侧的人群。

derivatives.zh: 由 parade 加 -ing 构成，指列队行进或刻意展示的行为
由 parade 加 -er 构成，指参加游行的人，也指爱炫耀的人
由 parade 与 ground 复合而成，指士兵操练、受阅的场地

senses.title: A public procession
senses.definition: an organized public march or procession, often with music, costumes and decorated vehicles, held to celebrate an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的公众行进，常配音乐、服装与彩车，用来庆祝某个日子
senses.example: The whole town turned out to watch the parade pass the old town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 全城人都出来看队伍经过旧市政厅。
senses.why: The word is generally traced through French to a Spanish noun for the place where soldiers halted and formed up; from troops gathering in the street it widened to any organized procession.
senses.whyCN: 一般认为这个词经法语来自西班牙语中表示「士兵停下集合之处」的名词；从军队在街上集合，词义扩大为任何有组织的公众行进。

senses.title: A formal march of troops
senses.definition: a ceremony in which soldiers march in formation past a reviewing officer or a public stand
senses.definitionCN: 士兵列队走过检阅官或观礼台的仪式
senses.example: The general watched the parade from a raised platform.
senses.exampleCN: 将军站在检阅台上观看阅兵。
senses.why: Since the earliest parade was simply soldiers standing ready in one place, the military review is the oldest thread, and flags and formation still carry the sense of being inspected.
senses.whyCN: 既然最早的 parade 只是士兵在一处站好待命，阅兵就是最古老的一条线；旗帜与队形至今仍带着「接受检阅」的意味。

senses.title: A display meant to impress
senses.definition: an ostentatious show of wealth, skills or opinions intended to impress other people
senses.definitionCN: 为给人留下印象而摆出的财富、本领或主张
senses.example: His charity work was a parade of good intentions rather than real help.
senses.exampleCN: 他的慈善活动只是把好意摆出来给人看，并没有真正帮上忙。
senses.why: A procession exists to be watched, so when the watching matters more than the marching, the word slides into showing off.
senses.whyCN: 游行本来就是给人看的，一旦「被看见」比「行进」本身更重要，这个词就滑向了炫耀。

senses.title: To march in formation
