senses.definition: to walk or march in an ordered group, especially as part of a ceremony or in order to be seen
senses.definitionCN: 排成整齐的队伍行走，尤指作为仪式的一部分或为了被人看见
senses.example: The children paraded around the playground with paper flags.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们举着纸旗在操场上列队走了一圈。
senses.why: The verb simply sets the procession moving: the same ordered line, now seen as an action instead of a spectacle.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是让那支队伍动起来：同样整齐的一列，从眼前的场面变成了正在进行的动作。

intro.en: Parade is usually traced through French to a Spanish noun for a halting place, with the Latin verb parare, to make ready, at the far end; the showy sense came later.
intro.cn: 一般认为 parade 经法语上溯到西班牙语中表示「停下之处」的名词，最远处是拉丁语动词 parare（准备、使就绪）；「炫耀」义出现得较晚。

items.en: Parare meant to prepare or make ready, and its family spread through the Romance languages with senses of stopping and standing.
items.cn: parare 意为准备、使就绪，这一族词在罗曼语中扩散，带上停下、站定的意思。

items.en: Spanish parada named a halt or the place where troops stopped and formed up, from the verb parar, to stop.
items.cn: 西班牙语 parada 指停下的动作或士兵停下集合的地方，来自动词 parar（停下）。

items.en: French took the word as parade and used it for a setting out of troops and for a showy display.
items.cn: 法语借入后写作 parade，用来指军队列队出场，也指铺张的展示。

items.en: English borrowed parade for a military muster and for the ground where soldiers assembled.
items.cn: 英语借入 parade，指军队集合检阅，也指士兵集合的场地。

items.en: Modern English keeps the military review, the civic procession and the showy display, and uses the verb for marching and for showing off.
items.cn: 现代英语保留阅兵、市民游行与炫耀三层意思，动词则用于列队行进和炫耀。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Spanish and Latin words behind the term, plus two spellings that only resemble it; the near-meaning group follows processions, marches and displays.
note.cn: 形近组沿这个词背后的西班牙语与拉丁语词展开，另收两个只是拼写相像的词；近义组收游行、行进与展示。

entries.definition: A halt, or the place where troops stand ready; the Spanish noun behind the English word.
entries.definitionCN: 停下，或士兵站好待命之处；英语词背后的西班牙语名词。

entries.definition: To stop or to halt, the verb that produced the noun parada.
entries.definitionCN: 停下、止住，是造出名词 parada 的动词。

entries.definition: A comic imitation of a style or a work; it merely looks like parade and comes from other roots.
entries.definitionCN: 对某种风格或作品的滑稽模仿；只是拼写与 parade 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A typical example or a pattern of thinking; the spelling is close but the Greek roots are unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 典型范例或思维模式；拼写相近，但希腊词根与 parade 无关。

entries.definition: A line of people or vehicles moving forward as part of a ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 仪式中向前行进的一队人或车辆。

entries.definition: To walk with regular steps, especially as a group.
entries.definitionCN: 有节奏地行走，尤指成群行进。

entries.definition: A public show with costumes and scenes, often outdoors.
entries.definitionCN: 常为户外的、带服装与场景的公众表演。

entries.definition: An arrangement or show intended to be looked at.
entries.definitionCN: 摆出来供人观看的展示。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a place where troops stood ready and became a line of people made to be watched; the family around it keeps those two ideas.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从士兵站好待命的地方开始，变成一列特意给人看的队伍；周围的词族一直带着这两个念头。

normal.en: The word is generally traced to Spanish parada, a halt where troops formed up, so the military sense is the oldest.
normal.cn: 一般认为这个词来自西班牙语 parada，即部队停下集合之处，所以军事义最古老。

normal.en: French parade added the idea of a show, which is why a fashion parade is about being watched rather than walking.
normal.cn: 法语 parade 加进了「展示」的意思，所以 fashion parade 的重点是被看，而不是走路。

normal.en: The verb is regular: parades, paraded, parading, with no change of vowel.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：parades、paraded、parading，元音不变。

normal.en: On parade means soldiers are lined up for inspection, not simply walking down a street.
normal.cn: on parade 指士兵列队接受检阅，并不是单纯在街上走。

normal.en: To rain on someone's parade is to spoil a moment that was arranged to be enjoyed in public.
normal.cn: rain on someone's parade 就是破坏一个本来要当众享受的时刻。

abstract.en: A parade turns a street into a stage, and everyone on it is at once performer and audience.
abstract.cn: 游行把街道变成舞台，走在上面的人既是演员也是观众。

abstract.en: A show of strength is still a show, and the word keeps that suspicion that display is not the same as substance.
abstract.cn: 力量的展示终究还是展示，这个词一直保留着「排场不等于实力」的疑虑。

abstract.en: Soldiers standing ready and a band walking past share one name because both are meant to be seen by someone in authority.
abstract.cn: 站好待命的士兵与走过的乐队共用一个词，因为两者都要让有权看的人看见。

examples.en: The whole town turned out to watch the parade pass the old town hall.
examples.cn: 全城人都出来看队伍经过旧市政厅。

examples.en: The general watched the parade from a raised platform.
examples.cn: 将军站在检阅台上观看阅兵。

examples.en: The children paraded around the playground with paper flags.
examples.cn: 孩子们举着纸旗在操场上列队走了一圈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕累的」——游行队伍走得太久也会怕累的；记住 parade 是游行。

root: 一般认为经法语 parade 来自西班牙语 parada（停下集合之处），源于拉丁语 parare（准备、使就绪）：士兵站好待命的地方，后来成了给人看的队伍。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an ordered line of people meant to be seen; the senses run from a civic celebration to a military review, to a showing off, and finally to the act of marching.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一列特意给人看的整齐队伍；义项从市民庆祝走到阅兵、炫耀，最后落到列队行进这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a band and a line of marchers filling the street while the crowd leans forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：鼓乐队与一列行进的队伍占满街道，人群向前倾身观看。

branches.en: a band leading children down the main street
branches.cn: 鼓乐队带着孩子走过主街

branches.en: soldiers in step before a reviewing stand
branches.cn: 士兵在检阅台前齐步走过

branches.en: a borrowed car shown off at a party
branches.cn: 聚会上炫耀借来的车

branches.en: paper flags waving above a playground
branches.cn: 操场上挥动的纸旗

branches.en: boots striking the ground in one rhythm
branches.cn: 靴子以同一个节奏踏在地上

intro.en: The word is a Romance borrowing, and the pieces that built it are a Latin verb of preparing, a Spanish noun of halting, and a French noun of showing.
intro.cn: 这个词是罗曼语借词，构成它的部件是一个表示准备的拉丁动词、一个表示停下的西班牙名词和一个表示展示的法语名词。

latinIntro.en: A Latin verb is recorded behind this word: parare, to make ready, which passed into Spanish as parar and gave the noun parada.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后有一个可考的拉丁动词 parare（准备、使就绪），它进入西班牙语成为 parar，并造出名词 parada。

items.meaning: a show, a setting out of troops
the act of marching or showing off
items.meaningCN: 列队行进或炫耀的行为

definition_zh: 有效的；正当的；有根据的；合法的
definition_en: able to be legally used, based on sound reasoning, or accepted as true
core_image: 检票闸机亮起绿灯，车票被放行
scene: 车站闸机前，他把票贴上去，绿灯亮起，挡板轻轻一响才打开。 Your ticket is valid for two hours after you buy it.
sceneCN: 这里 valid 是「有效的」（第 1 个义项：在规则上能用）；句意为车票购买后两小时内有效。闸机亮起绿灯的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ity 构成名词，义为「有效性；合法性」
加 -ate 构成动词，义为「使有效；验证」
加否定前缀 in-，义为「无效的」
加 -ation 构成名词，义为「验证；确认」

senses.title: Legally or officially acceptable
senses.definition: accepted by law or by rules for a certain period
senses.definitionCN: 被法律或规则认可，并在一定期限内可用
senses.example: This passport is valid for another three years.
senses.exampleCN: 这本护照还有三年有效期。
senses.why: The Latin adjective means strong; a paper that is strong by the rules is one the gate must let through.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词本义是「强的」；一份按规矩站得住的证件，就是闸机必须放行的证件。

senses.title: Based on sound reasoning
senses.definition: of an argument or point, sound and hard to attack
senses.definitionCN: 形容论点扎实、难以反驳
senses.example: Her objection was valid and changed the design.
senses.exampleCN: 她的反对意见有道理，设计因此改了。
senses.why: An argument that stands up to attack is strong in the same sense, so the word moves from papers to reasons.
senses.whyCN: 经得住反驳的论证同样「强」，于是词义从证件挪到了理由上。

senses.title: Accepted as true after checking
senses.definition: of a result or method, confirmed as sound by tests
senses.definitionCN: 形容结果或方法经过检验而被确认可靠
senses.example: The experiment was repeated and the result remained valid.
senses.exampleCN: 实验被重复了一次，结果依然成立。
senses.why: What survives a test is strong in the same root sense, so the word moves from gates and courts into the lab.
senses.whyCN: 经得住反复检验的东西同样「强」，于是词义又从闸机和法庭走进了实验室。

senses.title: A good and acceptable reason
senses.definition: of a reason or excuse, good enough to be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 形容理由或借口足以被人接受
senses.example: He had a valid reason for missing the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他缺席会议有正当理由。
senses.why: A reason that holds up when others look at it works like a valid paper: it passes, so it must be accepted.
senses.whyCN: 理由经人一看仍站得住，就同一份有效的文书一样能过关，因而必须被接受。

intro.en: A Latin adjective of strength, borrowed whole, whose root also gives value and valour.
intro.cn: 一个整体借入的、表示「强」的拉丁形容词，其词根也给出 value 与 valour。

items.en: Valere meant to be strong or to be worth, and validus meant strong and effective.
items.cn: valere 意为「强壮、有价值」，validus 意为「强壮的、有效的」。

items.en: Legal writers used validus of wills and contracts that had full force.
items.cn: 法律作者用 validus 来形容具有完全效力的遗嘱与契约。

items.en: English adopts the word in the sixteenth century from Latin legal use.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从拉丁法律用语中采用这个词。

items.en: The sense spreads from documents to arguments and reasons that hold up.
items.cn: 词义从文书扩展到经得住推敲的论证与理由。

items.en: Validity, validate, and invalid complete the modern family.
items.cn: validity、validate 与 invalid 补全了现代词族。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the val- family of strength and worth, and the near-meaning group sets effective against void.
note.cn: 形近组收集表示「强、值」的 val- 词族，近义组把有效与作废相对照。

entries.definition: low land between hills, only the opening is close, the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 山谷；只是词头相近，词源不同

normalIntro.en: Hold the root idea of strength: what is valid stands up, in law, in argument, or under test.
normalIntro.cn: 记住「强」这个根义：valid 的东西站得住，无论在法律上、论证里还是检验中。

normal.en: A ticket is valid for a period, so the preposition is for.
normal.cn: 车票的有效期用 for 表示。

normal.en: The negative is invalid, made with in-.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 invalid，用 in- 构成。

normal.en: Validate is what a system does to the password you type.
normal.cn: validate 就是系统对你输入的密码所做的事。

normal.en: A valid point in a meeting is an argument that holds.
normal.cn: 会上的 a valid point 指站得住的论点。

normal.en: Value and valid share one root: strength and worth.
normal.cn: value 与 valid 同根：强与值。

abstract.en: Picture a gate lamp turning green as a ticket is read.
abstract.cn: 想象读票时闸机灯变绿。

abstract.en: See a stamp with a date that has just run out.
abstract.cn: 看一枚日期刚过的印章。

abstract.en: Hear a quiet objection that no one in the room can answer.
abstract.cn: 听一句无人能答复的低声反对。

examples.en: The pass is valid on all city buses until midnight.
examples.cn: 这张通行证在午夜前可用于所有市内公交。

examples.en: She raised a valid point about the cost of the plan.
examples.cn: 她就计划成本提出了一个站得住脚的意见。

examples.en: The results were checked twice and are still valid.
examples.cn: 结果核验了两次，依然成立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威力的」——有威力的东西自然有效力。

root: 拉丁语 valere（强壮、有价值）的形容词 validus（强壮的、有效的），进入英语为 valid

sensesIntro.en: A root of strength spreads into legal force, sound reasoning, tested results, and reasons good enough to be accepted.
sensesIntro.cn: 「强」这个词根延伸到法律效力、论证扎实、经检验的结果以及够格的正当理由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate lamp turning green for a ticket.
core.cn: 核心意象：闸机为一张票亮起绿灯。

branches.en: The legal branch: the rule still lets it pass.
branches.cn: 法律分支：规则仍然允许通过。

branches.en: The argument branch: it holds up under attack.
branches.cn: 论证分支：经受得住反驳。

branches.en: The test branch: it survives a repeat check.
branches.cn: 检验分支：重复检验后仍然成立。

branches.en: The reason branch: good enough to be accepted.
branches.cn: 理由分支：够格被人接受。

branches.en: The force branch: valid always means it can be relied on.
branches.cn: 效力分支：有效总意味着可以依靠。

intro.en: A Latin adjective of strength with an adjective ending, closely tied to value and valour.
intro.cn: 一个表示「强」的拉丁形容词加形容词词尾，与 value、valour 紧密相关。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere meant to be strong or to be worth, and validus meant strong; value and valour belong to the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere 意为「强壮、有价值」，validus 意为「强壮的」；value 与 valour 同属这一词族。

items.example: The root val- joins strength with worth.
items.exampleCN: 词根 val- 把强壮与价值连在一起。

items.example: Validate means to make or prove valid.
items.exampleCN: validate 意为使有效或加以证实。

items.example: Valour shares the root of strength.
Value keeps the worth side of the root.
items.exampleCN: value 保留了词根中「价值」的一面。

latinEntries.meaning: to be strong, to be worth

definition_zh: 人工地；人造地；不自然地
definition_en: by human effort rather than natural processes, or in an affected way
core_image: 实验室里调出的甜味，不像树上长出来的
scene: 饮料瓶上印着零糖，喝起来却甜。 The drink is artificially sweetened.
sceneCN: 这里 artificially 是「人工地」（第 1 个义项：靠人工手段而非自然生成）；句意是这饮料用人工甜味剂增甜。

derivatives.zh: 名词：人造的性质；不自然

senses.title: By human means
senses.definition: by human skill or industry rather than by natural processes
senses.definitionCN: 靠人的技术或生产，而不是自然生成
senses.example: The lake is artificially filled each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这个湖每年夏天靠人工注水。
senses.why: Artificial joins ars 'skill' and facere 'to make', so artificially marks what is made by skill rather than grown by nature.
senses.whyCN: artificial 由 ars（技艺）与 facere（做）合成，本义是「用技艺做出来的」，加 -ly 后表示以人工方式完成，与自然形成相对。

senses.title: In an affected way
senses.definition: in a way that is not sincere or natural
senses.definitionCN: 显得做作、不真诚
senses.example: He smiled artificially at the guest.
senses.exampleCN: 他对客人不自然地笑了笑。
senses.why: A made thing has no trace of natural growth; that feature moves from objects to manners, so the adverb can describe a forced smile.
senses.whyCN: 人工制品没有自然生长的痕迹，这个「非自然」的特点从物转到神态，就表示刻意做作、不真诚。

intro.en: Artificially is the adverb of artificial, a Latin loanword built on skill and making.
intro.cn: artificially 是 artificial 的副词形式，而 artificial 是建立在「技艺」与「制作」之上的拉丁借词。

items.en: ars meant 'skill, craft or art'.
items.cn: ars 意为「技艺、手艺」。

items.en: facere meant 'to make or do'.
items.cn: facere 意为「制作、做」。

items.en: artificialis meant 'made by art or skill'.
items.cn: artificialis 意为「由技艺做成的」。

items.en: English took artificial to mean made by human skill, not by nature.
items.cn: 英语借入 artificial，指由人的技艺造成、而非自然生成。

items.en: The suffix -ly produced the adverb, which also came to describe an affected manner.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 构成副词，后来也用来形容做作的神态。

note.en: The look-alike group is the artificial family; the near-meaning group covers unnatural and synthetic ways.
note.cn: 形近组是 artificial 词族；近义组是表示不自然与合成的副词。

normalIntro.en: The adverb points to the maker behind the thing.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词指向事物背后的人为制造。

normal.en: It is adverbial, so it usually sits before the participle it modifies.
normal.cn: 它是副词，通常放在所修饰的分词之前。

normal.en: Pair it with food and light: artificially sweetened, artificial light.
normal.cn: 常与食物和光搭配：人工增甜、人造光。

normal.en: The base adjective ends in -ial, the adverb keeps the whole stem and adds -ly.
normal.cn: 形容词以 -ial 结尾，变副词时保留整个词干再加 -ly。

normal.en: In the manner sense it suggests something forced.
normal.cn: 表示神态时，它暗示刻意用力。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with artfully, which means cleverly.
normal.cn: 不要与 artfully 混淆，后者是「巧妙地」。

abstract.en: See a can of soda sweating on a shelf, its sweetness invented.
abstract.cn: 想象货架上冒汗的汽水罐，甜味是调出来的。

abstract.en: See a greenhouse where nothing grew from seed.
abstract.cn: 想象一座没有一粒种子发芽的温室。

abstract.en: See a smile that stops before it reaches the eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一个还没到眼睛就停住的笑容。

examples.en: The lake is artificially filled each summer.
examples.cn: 这个湖每年夏天靠人工注水。

examples.en: He smiled artificially at the guest.
examples.cn: 他对客人不自然地笑了笑。

examples.en: These flavours are artificially produced in a factory.
examples.cn: 这些风味是在工厂里人工合成的。

dict_mnemonic.text: artificial（人工的）加 -ly 成副词：以人工方式做，或显得不自然。

root: artificial 源自拉丁语 ars「技艺」与 facere「做」，本义「用技艺做出来的」，加 -ly 构成副词，表示靠人工而非自然，也可指神态做作。

sensesIntro.en: One sense concerns who makes a thing; the other concerns how a person behaves.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项问东西由谁造成，另一个义项看人的举止是否自然。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sweet taste blended in a lab, not grown on a tree.
core.cn: 核心意象：甜味在实验室里调配出来，不是树上长出来的。

branches.en: artificially sweetened
branches.cn: 人工增甜的

branches.en: artificially low
branches.cn: 人为压低的

branches.en: artificially created
branches.cn: 人工制造的

branches.en: smile artificially
branches.cn: 不自然地笑

branches.en: an artificially warm voice
branches.cn: 刻意堆出的热情嗓音

intro.en: The word is built from skill and making, and it gathers a whole family of Latin-rooted forms.
intro.cn: 这个词由「技艺」与「制作」构成，并带出一整族拉丁词根词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin roots ars and facere also gave artifice, artifact and artisan.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 ars 与 facere 还产生了 artifice、artifact 与 artisan。

definition_zh: 计算；估算；用计算机运算
definition_en: to calculate an amount or result using numbers or a computer
core_image: 手指在算盘上一颗颗拨珠，数字在脑中排成队
scene: 他用纸笔把每个月的开销一笔笔算出来。 She computed the total cost before booking the tickets.
sceneCN: 这里 compute 指「计算」（第 1 个义项：用数字算出结果）；句意是她在订票前算出了总费用。

pos.zh: 计算；估算；用计算机运算

senses.title: Work out with numbers
senses.definition: to calculate an amount or result using numbers
senses.definitionCN: 用数字算出数量或结果
senses.example: He computed the distance in his head.
senses.exampleCN: 他在脑子里算出了距离。
senses.why: The oldest sense is counting and reckoning with figures.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是数数并用数字推算。

senses.title: Process data by machine
senses.definition: to use a computer to process data and produce results
senses.definitionCN: 用计算机处理数据并得出结果
senses.example: The program computes the results in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序几秒钟就算出结果。
senses.why: A machine now does the old human work of reckoning, only faster.
senses.whyCN: 机器如今替人完成古老的推算工作，只是更快。

intro.en: Compute comes from Latin computare, to reckon together, built from com-, together, and putare, to count.
intro.cn: compute 来自拉丁语 computare（一起估算），由 com-（一起）与 putare（计数）构成。

items.en: Putare meant to count, to think over or to prune.
items.cn: putare 意为计数、思考或修剪。

items.en: Computare meant to add up and settle an account.
items.cn: computare 意为加总并结清账目。

items.en: Old French computer carried the word into bookkeeping.
items.cn: 古法语 computer 把这个词带入记账。

items.en: English compute meant to reckon or to estimate by figures.
items.cn: 英语 compute 意为用数字推算或估算。

items.en: The word gave birth to computer and to modern computing.
items.cn: 这个词后来衍生出 computer 与现代计算技术。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to compute, and the meaning group names other words for working out a figure.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 compute 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示算出数字的词。

entries.definition: a machine that stores and processes data
to work out a number using figures

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with beads on an abacus, then move to machines that reckon in seconds.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从算盘上的珠子开始，再走到几秒钟就能算完的机器。

normal.en: Com- is together and putare is to count, so compute is to count things together.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，putare 是计数，compute 就是把数字合起来算。

normal.en: A computer is simply a thing that computes.
normal.cn: computer 不过就是会 compute 的东西。

normal.en: Compute is the verb, computation is the noun, computer is the tool.
normal.cn: compute 是动词，computation 是名词，computer 是工具。

normal.en: You can compute in your head without any machine.
normal.cn: 不用任何机器，你也能在脑子里计算。

normal.en: The result is computed, not guessed.
normal.cn: 结果是算出来的，不是猜出来的。

abstract.en: Picture fingers moving beads along thin wires.
abstract.cn: 想象手指在细杆上拨动珠子。

abstract.en: Picture a column of figures adding into one line.
abstract.cn: 想象一列数字加总成一行。

abstract.en: Picture a small chip finishing a long sum instantly.
abstract.cn: 想象一块小芯片瞬间算完一长串加法。

examples.en: The software computes the average in a second.
examples.cn: 这个软件一秒钟就算出平均值。

examples.en: We computed the cost of the whole trip.
examples.cn: 我们算出了整趟旅行的费用。

examples.en: Early machines could compute only simple sums.
examples.cn: 早期的机器只能计算简单的加法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compute 记成 com（一起）加 put（计算）：把数字合在一起算，就是计算。

root: 源自拉丁语 computare（com 一起 + putare 计数），本义是加总结账，后指一般意义上的计算与估算，并衍生出 computer 一词。

sensesIntro.en: From a person reckoning with figures, to a machine processing data in the same spirit.
sensesIntro.cn: 从人用数字推算，到机器以同样的精神处理数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers moving beads on an abacus while numbers line up in the mind.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指拨动算盘珠，数字在脑中排成队。

branches.en: Human reckoning is the ancient core of the word.
branches.cn: 人的推算是这个词古老的核心。

branches.en: The machine sense is the same act handed to silicon.
branches.cn: 机器义项只是把同一个动作交给芯片。

branches.en: Mental arithmetic needs no device at all.
branches.cn: 心算完全不需要任何设备。

branches.en: Modern computing extends the old verb to data of every kind.
branches.cn: 现代计算把这个古老动词扩展到各类数据。

branches.en: Both senses turn numbers into an answer.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把数字变成一个答案。

intro.en: Compute is built on Latin com-, together, plus putare, to count or reckon.
intro.cn: compute 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 putare（计数）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base put- also gives reputation, dispute and impute.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 put- 还给出 reputation、dispute 与 impute。

items.example: The app computes the shortest route.
items.exampleCN: 这个应用算出最短路线。
云计算改变了这个行业。

items.example: The computer needs a new battery.

items.exampleCN: 这项运算花了两个小时。
他们建立了一个计算模型。

items.example: The first microcomputer appeared in the 1970s.
items.exampleCN: 第一台微型计算机出现在二十世纪七十年代。
